item.content:encoded:
The University of Macau (UM) is preparing to welcome applications for its 2027/2028 postgraduate intake, providing prospective students with opportunities to pursue doctoral, master’s and postgraduate certificate programmes in Macau, China.

For applicants seeking postgraduate study in China, the intake provides an opportunity to explore a wide range of academic programmes while also considering available funding and assistantship opportunities.

Important: The source information describes these as postgraduate opportunities with potential funding. Applicants should not assume that every programme is fully funded. Funding availability depends on the programme and applicable scholarship or assistantship conditions.

About the University of Macau Postgraduate Intake

The University of Macau offers postgraduate education through its various academic units, including PhD, Master’s and postgraduate certificate programmes.

Applicants can submit their applications through the university’s official online application system. The system specifically provides registration options for PhD and other doctoral degree, Master’s and postgraduate certificate programmes.

The university’s postgraduate programmes cover multiple academic and professional disciplines, giving prospective students the opportunity to identify programmes that align with their educational background and career goals.

Programmes Available

The 2027/2028 intake includes opportunities in three main categories:

1. PhD Programmes

Doctoral programmes are designed for students seeking advanced research training and an opportunity to develop expertise in their chosen field.

PhD applicants should carefully review the requirements of their intended academic unit because admission conditions can vary by programme.

2. Master’s Programmes

The University of Macau offers a range of master’s-level programmes across different faculties and academic areas.

Applicants generally need to hold a Bachelor’s degree or an academic qualification recognized as equivalent by the University of Macau, although individual programmes may have additional requirements.

3. Postgraduate Certificate Programmes

The intake also includes selected postgraduate certificate programmes. The university publishes programme-specific information covering areas such as the language of instruction and normal duration of study.

Funding Opportunities

One of the most attractive aspects of the University of Macau’s postgraduate opportunities is the availability of financial support for eligible students.

For doctoral students, the university’s published PhD admission guidelines identify the UM PhD Scholarship and UM PhD Teaching Research Assistant as potential sources of stipend support.

Assistantships are also available for master’s students and can serve as a source of stipend support, subject to the applicable funding guidelines.

However, applicants should distinguish between admission to a postgraduate programme and receiving funding. Funding is subject to the relevant programme, scholarship or assistantship conditions and should be confirmed before making financial plans.

Who Can Apply?

The exact eligibility requirements depend on the postgraduate programme selected.

For master’s applicants, the university’s published admission guidelines state that applicants must possess a Bachelor’s degree or an academic background recognized as equivalent by the University of Macau. Some programmes may require additional academic or professional qualifications.

PhD applicants should consult the specific admission guidelines and requirements for their intended doctoral programme.

International applicants should also carefully review the university’s requirements concerning:

  • Academic qualifications
  • English or other language proficiency
  • Programme-specific requirements
  • Supporting documents
  • Application fees
  • Scholarship or assistantship eligibility
  • Any interview requirements

Application Deadlines

According to the information provided for the 2027/2028 intake, the key deadlines are:

PhD Programmes

First Batch Deadline: 23 October 2026

Master’s & Postgraduate Certificate Programmes

Deadline: 3 December 2026

Applicants should not wait until the final day to begin the application process because documents, references and other supporting materials may require additional preparation.

The University of Macau also states that late applications will not be considered and that completed online applications must be submitted through the application system to be processed.

How to Apply

Applications are submitted online through the University of Macau’s official application system.

The process generally involves:

Step 1: Register an Account

New applicants should select the registration option for PhD and other doctoral degree, Master’s and postgraduate certificate programmes.

Applicants are required to provide information including their name as shown on their identification document or passport, identification/passport number, mobile number and valid email address.

Step 2: Receive Your Login Details

After successful registration, applicants receive a reference number and password by email and SMS. These details are required to access the application system.

Step 3: Complete the Application

Applicants should carefully complete the online application form and provide all required information and supporting documents.

Step 4: Submit the Application

Completing the form is not enough. Applicants must click Submit for the application to be processed.

The university states that applications that have been completed but not submitted will not be processed. (UM Sign In)

Step 5: Check for Confirmation

Successful submission should generate an acknowledgement email containing an application number. The university advises applicants to contact the Graduate School if they do not receive the acknowledgement within two days. (UM Sign In)

Application Fee

Applicants should also budget for the postgraduate application fee.

The University of Macau’s published admission rules state that the application fee is MOP 200 per application and is non-refundable.

Applicants should check the applicable admission guidelines for their specific intake and programme before making payment.

Important Application Considerations

Review Your Programme Carefully

Applicants should choose their programme carefully because the university’s online application instructions state that applicants for PhD, master’s and postgraduate certificate programmes cannot change their programme choice after submitting their applications.

Prepare Documents Early

Potential applicants should begin preparing their academic records, identification documents, language certificates, recommendation materials and other programme-specific documents well ahead of the deadline.

Check Funding Separately

Do not automatically assume that admission to a programme means that tuition and living expenses will be fully covered.

Applicants interested in funding should review the specific scholarship or assistantship opportunities associated with their programme.

Monitor Your Email

The university uses email to provide important application information, including registration credentials and application acknowledgement.

Why Consider the University of Macau?

For students considering postgraduate education in Asia, the University of Macau provides an opportunity to pursue advanced academic study in an internationally oriented university environment.

The availability of doctoral scholarships and teaching/research assistantships may also make selected postgraduate programmes particularly attractive to applicants seeking financial support.

However, applicants should evaluate each programme individually, including its academic requirements, tuition fees, funding options, language requirements and career relevance.

Application Timeline at a Glance

Programme Intake Deadline
PhD 2027/2028 23 October 2026 – First Batch
Master’s 2027/2028 3 December 2026
Postgraduate Certificate 2027/2028 3 December 2026

Conclusion

The University of Macau 2027/2028 postgraduate intake offers prospective students an opportunity to pursue PhD, Master’s and postgraduate certificate programmes in Macau, China.

With applications opening for different postgraduate categories and potential financial support available through scholarships and assistantships, prospective students should begin researching suitable programmes and preparing their applications early.

The most important step is to review the requirements and funding conditions for your chosen programme directly through the University of Macau before submitting an application.

Official University Information: University of Macau

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
Applications for the 2027 Switzer Fellowship will open in September 2026, offering graduate students in the United States and U.S. territories an opportunity to receive an $18,000 unrestricted cash award, leadership training, career support, and access to a professional network of more than 800 environmental leaders.

The fellowship is designed for graduate students whose academic and career goals focus on environmental improvement and who demonstrate leadership, applied problem-solving, interdisciplinary collaboration, and a commitment to advancing social equity through environmental work.

About the Switzer Fellowship

The Switzer Fellowship is a one-year graduate fellowship supporting emerging and established environmental leaders across a broad range of disciplines.

Switzer Fellows work in areas including:

  • Environmental science
  • Public policy
  • Environmental justice
  • Public health
  • Economics
  • Advocacy
  • Planning
  • Business
  • Law
  • Research and academia

The fellowship welcomes applicants from diverse academic, professional, social and economic backgrounds, particularly those who are committed to interdisciplinary approaches, practical environmental solutions, collaborative leadership and social equity.

For the 2027 fellowship cycle, the programme has expanded nationwide and is no longer restricted to applicants studying in New England or California.

What Does the Switzer Fellowship Provide?

Selected fellows receive an $18,000 unrestricted cash award, paid in two installments in June and January.

The fellowship also provides opportunities for:

1. Leadership Development

Fellows participate in two multi-day retreats focused on cohort building, networking, equity-centered leadership and professional skills development.

2. Career Coaching

Switzer Fellows have access to career coaching and leadership guidance during their fellowship year and beyond. The Foundation helps fellows identify leadership opportunities and establish connections throughout the Switzer Network.

3. Switzer Network Membership

One of the major advantages of the fellowship is lifelong access to the Switzer Network, a community of more than 800 fellows selected since 1986.

Network activities include:

  • Professional networking events
  • Job and information sharing
  • Webinars and training
  • Social gatherings
  • Professional development opportunities
  • Additional grant opportunities

 

4. Future Grant Opportunities

After completing the fellowship year, fellows can access additional grant programmes designed to strengthen leadership and professional development, including leadership and professional development grants.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must meet the Switzer Fellowship’s eligibility requirements.

To qualify, applicants must:

  • Be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, DACA recipient, refugee or asylee according to the specified U.S. Department of Homeland Security definition.
  • Be enrolled in an accredited graduate institution in the United States or U.S. territories.
  • Not be enrolled in an online programme.
  • Plan to remain enrolled throughout the entire 2027–2028 academic year.
  • Have strong academic qualifications and academic and career goals focused on environmental improvement.

Requirements for Master’s Students

Master’s degree candidates, including J.D. students, must have completed at least one semester or quarter of coursework when applying and must be pursuing the Master’s degree as their terminal degree.

Students planning to continue into a Ph.D. are advised to wait and apply once they are enrolled in their doctoral programme. Students entering a one-year Master’s programme may apply before enrollment, but they must have been formally accepted before they can be interviewed.

Requirements for Ph.D. Students

Ph.D. candidates must have completed their qualifying examinations by the time of application.

Mid-Career Applicants

Mid-career students are encouraged to apply. They must demonstrate how their academic programme will strengthen their effectiveness as environmental leaders.

Who Is Especially Encouraged to Apply?

The Switzer Foundation particularly encourages applications from:

  • Black students
  • Indigenous students
  • Students of color
  • First-generation college students
  • Individuals from groups traditionally underrepresented in environmental graduate programmes
  • Students from a wide range of universities, including state universities

 

How Are Fellows Selected?

The Foundation selects approximately 20 fellows each year from hundreds of applicants.

Applications are assessed according to several criteria, including:

  1. Environmental commitment
  2. Applied focus
  3. Innovative problem-solving
  4. Leadership potential
  5. Collaboration and engagement
  6. Social equity awareness and experience
  7. Communication skills

 

Successful candidates should therefore demonstrate more than strong academic performance. Their applications should clearly show how their environmental work addresses practical problems and affects human communities.

Ph.D. applicants are expected to have a clearly defined research focus and explain how their academic goals can contribute to positive change in applied environmental problems.

Application Review Process

After an initial eligibility review, applications go through three rounds of review by Switzer Fellowship alumni.

The alumni reviewers are selected to provide broad representation across areas such as:

  • Race
  • Gender
  • Educational background
  • Degree programme
  • Professional sector
  • Fellowship cohort
  • Geography

 

Selected applicants participate in a virtual panel interview in May with Switzer Foundation fellows and representatives. Award decisions are communicated in writing within two weeks following the interviews.

2027 Application Timeline

The application timeline provided by the Switzer Foundation is:

Applications open: September 2026

Interviews: Early May

Award notifications: June

 

Application deadline: The source currently states that applications will begin being accepted in September 2026 but does not provide a specific closing date. Applicants should therefore check the official application page once the 2027 application cycle opens.

Fellowship Responsibilities

Being selected as a Switzer Fellow comes with participation requirements.

Attend Two Retreats

All fellows must attend two multi-day, in-person retreats held in September and April during the fellowship year.

The retreats focus on:

  • Cohort building
  • Networking
  • Equity-centered leadership
  • Skills development

 

Participate in the Switzer Network

Fellows are expected to remain active members of the Switzer Network during and after their fellowship year.

Participation can include:

  • Attending or hosting networking events
  • Participating in network discussions
  • Coaching earlier-career fellows
  • Serving on the Fellows Advisory Committee
  • Participating in the selection of future fellows

 

Submit a Fellowship Report

Fellows must submit a brief written report at the conclusion of their fellowship year. An optional interim report may also be requested in January.

How Can the $18,000 Award Be Used?

The unrestricted fellowship award may be used for one or more of the following:

  • Tuition
  • Matriculation and university fees
  • Living expenses
  • Education-related expenses
  • Research-related expenses

If the fellowship funds are not used for these purposes, they may be considered taxable income and the fellow may be responsible for applicable income tax.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Switzer Fellowship could be particularly relevant for graduate students who are developing solutions to environmental challenges and want to connect their work to broader social outcomes.

Potential applicants may include students working on environmental problems related to:

  • Climate and environmental change
  • Environmental justice
  • Public health
  • Environmental policy
  • Sustainable development
  • Natural resources
  • Community resilience
  • Environmental planning
  • Environmental science and research

However, the fellowship is not restricted to a single academic discipline. The Foundation’s existing fellows work across science, policy, health, economics, advocacy, planning, business, law and other fields.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

If you intend to apply when applications open in September 2026, consider preparing early.

1. Clearly Explain Your Environmental Focus

Your application should make it easy for reviewers to understand the environmental problem you are addressing and why it matters.

2. Demonstrate Practical Impact

The Foundation places emphasis on applied environmental problem-solving. Explain how your research, studies or professional work can contribute to real-world solutions.

3. Highlight Leadership

Provide concrete examples showing how you have taken initiative, influenced others, collaborated with stakeholders or contributed to environmental change.

4. Connect Environment and Social Equity

Social equity is an important part of the Switzer Fellowship’s selection criteria. Applicants should clearly demonstrate how their environmental work affects people and communities.

5. Show Collaboration

The selection criteria include collaboration and engagement, so demonstrate your ability to work across disciplines, communities or professional sectors.

Important Exclusions

Employees and trustees of the Robert and Patricia Switzer Foundation, as well as their family members, are not eligible to apply.

The Foundation states that it does not discriminate in selection on the basis of race, color, gender, gender expression, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, or national or ethnic origin.

How to Apply

Applications for the 2027 Switzer Fellowship are scheduled to open in September 2026.

Applicants should use the official How to Apply information provided by the Switzer Network when the application window opens.

Applicants can also explore the Switzer Network and learn more about previous fellows to understand the range of environmental and social-impact work represented within the fellowship community.

Conclusion

The 2027 Switzer Fellowship provides an opportunity for graduate students in the United States and U.S. territories to develop as environmental leaders while receiving an $18,000 award, leadership development, career coaching, professional networking and access to a long-term community of environmental change-makers.

With only about 20 fellows selected each year, applicants should prepare carefully and demonstrate a clear connection between their academic or professional work, practical environmental problem-solving, leadership and social equity.

Applications are expected to open in September 2026, making this an opportunity prospective applicants should begin preparing for now.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
UNICEF is inviting qualified professionals to apply for the Mixed-Methods Impact Evaluation Consultant – Adolescent Girls & Violence Against Children consultancy within the UNICEF Evaluation Office (EO) in New York, United States. The opportunity is designed for an experienced impact evaluation specialist with strong expertise in quantitative and qualitative research, violence against children, adolescent girls, child protection, and rigorous evaluation methodologies.

The consultancy will be undertaken remotely, with travel to selected project locations when required, and will run for 12 months. The successful consultant will contribute to important UNICEF impact evaluation initiatives addressing issues such as child marriage, social norms, violence in and around schools, and the agency, health and wellbeing of adolescent girls.

This opportunity may be particularly relevant to experienced researchers, evaluators, development professionals, public health specialists, economists, social scientists, and policy experts who have a strong record of conducting rigorous impact evaluations in low-income settings.

Opportunity Overview

  • Organization: UNICEF
  • Office: UNICEF Evaluation Office (EO)
  • Position: Mixed-Methods Impact Evaluation Consultant – Adolescent Girls & Violence Against Children
  • Job Number: 595428
  • Contract Type: Consultant
  • Level: Consultancy
  • Duty Station: New York, United States
  • Work Arrangement: Remote, with travel to project locations
  • Duration: 12 months
  • Advertised: 28 August 2026
  • Application Deadline: 13 September 2026
  • Primary Language: English
  • Additional Languages: French, Spanish or Arabic are assets

About UNICEF

UNICEF works across more than 190 countries and territories to protect children’s rights, save children’s lives and support children and adolescents in reaching their full potential.

The organization works across a broad range of areas, including child protection, education, health, nutrition, water and sanitation, adolescent development, gender equality, social policy and humanitarian response.

The UNICEF Evaluation Office plays an important role in strengthening evidence-based decision-making throughout the organization. Its work supports organizational learning and accountability by helping UNICEF understand what works, what does not work, why interventions produce particular outcomes, and how programs can be improved.

Through its network of regional evaluation teams, the Evaluation Office supports UNICEF country offices in generating and using evidence to improve programs for vulnerable children and communities.

About the UNICEF Evaluation Office

The Evaluation Office is one of UNICEF’s core evidence functions. It is responsible for supporting high-quality evaluations that can improve organizational performance, accountability and learning.

The office conducts several types of evaluations, including:

  • Strategic global evaluations
  • Institutional effectiveness evaluations
  • Humanitarian evaluations
  • Impact evaluations
  • Demand-driven evaluations

The Evaluation Office also develops and promotes standards, guidelines, norms and processes designed to strengthen the quality and use of UNICEF evaluations.

A major focus is the generation of rigorous impact evidence that can help UNICEF understand whether interventions are actually producing meaningful changes in the lives of children and adolescents.

The organization has emphasized impact evaluation as an increasingly important function, particularly as governments, donors and development organizations face increasing pressure to demonstrate results and make effective use of limited financial resources.

What Is the Purpose of This Consultancy?

The successful consultant will support UNICEF’s work on several important impact evaluation initiatives involving adolescent girls, child marriage, social norms, violence against children and child protection.

The consultancy will primarily support the implementation of the Impact Catalyst Fund (ICF) thematic windows and the demand-driven evaluation portfolio under the Power4Girls initiative.

The consultant may also support the scoping, development and implementation of broader impact evaluation opportunities involving:

  • Adolescent girls
  • Violence against children
  • Child protection
  • Child marriage
  • Social norms
  • Violence in schools
  • Girls’ agency
  • Girls’ health and wellbeing

This means the position requires more than general research experience. The successful candidate should be capable of applying rigorous mixed-methods evaluation approaches to complex and sensitive issues affecting children and adolescents.

Key Areas of Work

The consultancy is connected to several significant UNICEF initiatives.

1. Impact Catalyst Fund

The Impact Catalyst Fund is a flagship initiative designed to strengthen UNICEF’s ability to generate rigorous impact evidence.

The first thematic window was developed through a partnership with the Global Program to End Child Marriage (GPECM), focusing on child marriage and social norms.

The consultant will support work associated with this thematic area and contribute to strengthening evidence around interventions designed to address child marriage and related social and behavioral factors.

2. Preventing Violence in, Through and Around Schools

A further Impact Catalyst Fund initiative is being launched in 2026 around Preventing Violence in, Through and Around Schools.

This work is being undertaken in partnership with the Safe to Learn Initiative and focuses on understanding approaches that can prevent violence affecting children in school-related environments.

The consultant may therefore be involved in evaluation activities examining interventions, outcomes and implementation processes related to violence prevention.

3. Power4Girls

The Evaluation Office is also working with UNICEF’s Adolescent Girls Hub on demand-driven impact evaluations under the Power4Girls initiative.

These evaluations focus on increasing girls’:

  • Agency
  • Health
  • Wellbeing

The consultant will support this portfolio and help generate evidence that can inform programs designed to improve outcomes for adolescent girls.

Why This Consultancy Is Important

Violence against children, child marriage and challenges affecting adolescent girls are complex development issues. Effective responses require strong evidence about which interventions work, for whom, under what circumstances and at what cost.

Impact evaluation can help answer these questions.

Through rigorous quantitative and qualitative research, the consultant will contribute to evidence that can potentially influence program design, implementation, resource allocation and policy decisions.

The work is therefore closely connected to UNICEF’s broader mission of promoting the rights, safety and wellbeing of every child.

Who Is UNICEF Looking For?

UNICEF is seeking a highly experienced impact evaluation professional with an advanced academic background and substantial practical experience in rigorous evaluations.

The successful candidate should be comfortable working with both quantitative and qualitative research methods and should have experience dealing with sensitive research involving children and adolescents.

The position requires a combination of academic knowledge, research experience, technical evaluation skills, subject-matter expertise and strong communication abilities.

Educational Requirements

Applicants must have an advanced university degree at Master’s level or above in a relevant field.

Acceptable areas of study include:

  • Economics
  • Public Health
  • Public Policy
  • Political Science
  • Evaluation
  • Development Studies
  • Sociology

Applicants should ensure that their academic background demonstrates clear relevance to impact evaluation, development research, public policy, social science, public health or a closely related discipline.

Professional Experience Requirements

Applicants must have more than five years of professional experience leading or contributing to rigorous impact evaluations.

The required experience should include involvement in areas such as:

  • Evaluation design
  • Evaluation preparation
  • Study implementation
  • Impact measurement
  • Quantitative research
  • Qualitative research
  • Data collection
  • Data analysis
  • Research in low-income settings

Experience should demonstrate the ability to contribute meaningfully to evaluations rather than simply having general administrative or program-support experience.

Candidates who have designed studies, managed field research, analyzed evaluation data or contributed to published evaluation findings may be particularly well positioned for this consultancy.

Experience With Violence Against Children Research

A major requirement is experience collecting primary data on violence against children.

Applicants should have experience using quantitative and/or qualitative methods to collect information relating to violence against children and should understand the ethical considerations involved in such research.

Because research involving children can involve significant safeguarding concerns, candidates should understand appropriate:

  • Research ethics
  • Child safeguarding procedures
  • Referral protocols
  • Human-subject protections
  • Sensitive data collection practices
  • Participant protection procedures

Applicants are also expected to have basic ethics certification for facilitating primary studies involving human subjects, such as a CITI certificate or a similar qualification.

This requirement is particularly important because research involving violence against children requires careful consideration of participant safety and confidentiality.

Knowledge of UNICEF’s Work

Candidates should be familiar with UNICEF’s programmatic mandate.

They should also understand evidence-generation standards and processes relevant to child-focused impact evaluations.

Experience working with UNICEF, United Nations agencies, international development organizations, governments, research institutions, NGOs or other organizations involved in child-focused development programs may be relevant, although applicants should ensure that their specific experience meets the stated requirements.

Technical Evaluation Skills

The successful candidate must demonstrate strong technical expertise in both quantitative and qualitative evaluation methods.

This includes methods used to:

  • Identify impacts
  • Measure impacts
  • Answer complementary evaluation questions
  • Understand implementation and contextual factors
  • Combine quantitative and qualitative evidence
  • Assess cost-effectiveness

The ability to work across different methodological approaches is particularly important because the consultancy specifically focuses on mixed-methods impact evaluation.

Statistical and Research Software Skills

Applicants should be proficient in relevant statistical and qualitative analysis software.

UNICEF specifically identifies experience with:

Quantitative analysis

  • Stata
  • R

Qualitative analysis

  • NVivo
  • ATLAS.ti

Candidates should be able to use appropriate software to manage, analyze and interpret research data and produce high-quality evaluation findings.

Subject-Matter Knowledge

Applicants should demonstrate current knowledge of evidence and research relating to:

  • Child marriage
  • Violence against children
  • Adolescent girls
  • Child protection
  • Social norms
  • Girls’ agency
  • Health and wellbeing
  • Violence prevention

This means applicants should be able to demonstrate more than general research experience. They should understand the existing evidence base and major research questions within these thematic areas.

Academic Publications

UNICEF also requests a demonstrated track record of authorship or co-authorship in peer-reviewed journals.

Applicants should therefore highlight relevant publications in their CV and, where appropriate, explain how their published research demonstrates expertise in impact evaluation, adolescent girls, violence against children, child protection, public health, development or related areas.

Language Requirements

English is required for this consultancy.

Knowledge of additional languages is considered an asset.

These include:

  • French
  • Spanish
  • Arabic

Strong written and spoken English will be particularly important because the consultant will be expected to analyze evidence, prepare reports, communicate technical findings and participate in consultations with multiple stakeholders.

Additional Desirable Skills

Beyond the minimum requirements, UNICEF identifies several additional capabilities that would strengthen an applicant’s profile.

Ability to work under tight deadlines

The consultant should be able to deliver data analysis and evaluation outputs within demanding timelines.

Impact evaluations often involve multiple stages, stakeholders and deliverables, making effective time management essential.

Multi-stakeholder coordination

The consultant should be comfortable working through multi-stakeholder consultative processes.

This can require coordinating with researchers, UNICEF teams, program specialists, implementing partners, government stakeholders and other relevant actors.

Communicating technical information

A particularly important skill is the ability to explain complex technical information to non-technical audiences.

The successful candidate should be able to translate statistical and evaluation findings into clear conclusions and recommendations that policymakers, program managers and other stakeholders can understand and use.

Strong writing and presentation skills

Excellent drafting and presentation skills in English are desirable.

Candidates should be capable of preparing clear technical documents, reports, presentations and other evaluation outputs.

International collaboration

The consultant should be willing and able to coordinate across different time zones.

The position may require collaboration with teams primarily located in:

  • Rome
  • Nairobi
  • Beirut
  • Kolkata

The identified impact evaluation locations include Beirut and Kolkata.

Work Arrangement and Duration

This is a 12-month consultancy.

The duty station is listed as New York, United States, but the position is described as remote, with travel to project locations.

Therefore, applicants should be prepared for remote international collaboration as well as potential travel connected with evaluation activities.

The role may require flexibility because teams and project locations are distributed across different geographic regions and time zones.

UNICEF Core Values

Applicants are expected to demonstrate alignment with UNICEF’s organizational values.

UNICEF identifies its Core Values as Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS).

These values underpin how UNICEF works and how it engages with children, communities, partners, colleagues and other stakeholders.

Candidates should therefore demonstrate professional conduct, integrity, accountability and a strong commitment to safeguarding and human rights.

Diversity and Inclusion

UNICEF states that it welcomes qualified candidates regardless of:

  • Race or ethnicity
  • Disability
  • Gender identity
  • Sexual orientation
  • Religion
  • Nationality
  • Socio-economic background
  • Minority status
  • Other personal status

The organization also encourages applications from people with disabilities, including neurodivergent applicants.

Reasonable accommodation may be available during the recruitment process for candidates with disabilities.

Applicants who require accommodation are encouraged to contact UNICEF through the appropriate accessibility channel on the UNICEF Careers webpage.

Safeguarding and Background Checks

Because this consultancy involves work related to children and potentially sensitive research topics, safeguarding is a particularly important aspect of the recruitment process.

UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy toward conduct that is incompatible with its aims and objectives.

This includes:

  • Sexual exploitation and abuse
  • Sexual harassment
  • Abuse of authority
  • Discrimination
  • Other misconduct

Selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

These checks may include verification of:

  • Academic credentials
  • Employment history
  • References
  • Other information necessary for the recruitment and safeguarding process

Selected candidates may also be required to provide additional information to facilitate the background-check process.

Documents Required to Apply

Qualified applicants are required to submit their application through UNICEF’s online Talent Management System (TMS) Here

The application should include the following:

1. Updated TMS Profile and CV

Applicants should ensure that their UNICEF TMS profile is complete and up to date.

The CV should clearly demonstrate:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Relevant professional experience
  • Impact evaluation experience
  • Research experience
  • Violence-against-children research experience
  • Technical software skills
  • Publications
  • Relevant language skills
  • International or low-income-setting experience

2. Cover Letter

Applicants should provide a cover letter explaining their suitability for the consultancy.

A strong cover letter should connect the applicant’s experience directly to the requirements of the position.

Candidates should emphasize their most relevant impact evaluation projects, methodological expertise, research publications and experience involving adolescent girls, violence against children or related themes.

3. Financial Proposal

A separate financial proposal is required.

UNICEF states that the financial proposal must be submitted using the specified template.

Applicants should therefore pay careful attention to the required format and avoid submitting the financial proposal in an alternative format if the official template is available.

Important Note About the Terms of Reference

The vacancy refers applicants to the complete Terms of Reference (TOR) for additional information about the consultancy.

Candidates should review the full TOR before submitting an application because the vacancy announcement may not contain every technical detail relating to the consultancy’s deliverables, methodology, timelines and responsibilities.

The vacancy also provides a financial proposal template that applicants are expected to use.

If the TOR or financial proposal documents cannot be downloaded through certain recruitment platforms, UNICEF advises applicants to visit its official vacancies page.

How to Apply

Applicants interested in the consultancy should:

  1. Review the vacancy and complete Terms of Reference carefully.
  2. Confirm that they meet the Master’s-level education requirement.
  3. Verify that they have more than five years of relevant impact evaluation experience.
  4. Ensure they can demonstrate experience in low-income settings.
  5. Review their experience with violence-against-children research and ethical data collection.
  6. Confirm proficiency in the required quantitative and qualitative analysis tools.
  7. Update their UNICEF TMS profile.
  8. Prepare an up-to-date CV.
  9. Prepare a tailored cover letter.
  10. Complete the required financial proposal template.
  11. Submit all required materials through UNICEF’s online recruitment portal before the deadline.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

13 September 2026, Eastern Daylight Time (EDT).

The position was advertised on 28 August 2026.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications, particularly because the application requires multiple documents, including a separate financial proposal.

For more information visit the UNICEF website HERE

More UNICEF opportunities are on the OFY Website HERE

Important Fraud Warning

UNICEF clearly states that it does not charge a processing fee at any stage of recruitment, selection or hiring.

Applicants should not be asked to pay money for:

  • Application processing
  • Interviews
  • Validation
  • Appointment
  • Training
  • Recruitment

UNICEF also states that it will not ask applicants for their bank account information during the recruitment process.

Applicants should be cautious of individuals or websites falsely claiming to represent UNICEF and requesting payment or sensitive financial information.

Selection Process

As with other UNICEF vacancies, all positions are advertised through the organization’s recruitment system.

Only candidates who are shortlisted will be contacted and advanced to the next stage of the selection process.

Meeting the minimum requirements does not automatically guarantee selection.

Candidates should therefore make sure their applications clearly demonstrate how their education, professional experience, research expertise, technical skills and publications correspond with the consultancy requirements.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This consultancy is particularly suited to experienced professionals working in areas such as:

  • Impact evaluation
  • Monitoring and evaluation
  • Development research
  • Economics
  • Public health
  • Public policy
  • Political science
  • Sociology
  • Development studies
  • Child protection
  • Adolescent development
  • Gender development
  • Social policy
  • Research and evidence generation
  • Violence prevention
  • Child marriage research

It is not primarily an entry-level opportunity. The requirement for more than five years of professional impact evaluation experience, combined with the advanced degree and technical research requirements, makes this a specialist consultancy aimed at experienced professionals.

How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Applications

Candidates should make their applications evidence-based and directly connected to the vacancy.

When preparing a CV and cover letter, applicants should consider highlighting:

  • Specific impact evaluations they have led or contributed to
  • Their role in evaluation design and implementation
  • Quantitative and qualitative methodologies they have used
  • Experience collecting primary data
  • Experience researching violence against children
  • Experience working with children or adolescents under appropriate ethical protocols
  • CITI or equivalent human-subject research certification
  • Experience in low-income settings
  • Experience with Stata or R
  • Experience with NVivo or ATLAS.ti
  • Relevant peer-reviewed publications
  • Research involving child marriage or social norms
  • Experience evaluating education or school-based interventions
  • Experience with adolescent girls’ programs
  • Cost-effectiveness or economic evaluation experience
  • Experience communicating technical findings to non-technical audiences
  • International and multi-stakeholder collaboration

Applicants should avoid relying on generic descriptions of their responsibilities. Instead, they should demonstrate measurable contributions and outcomes wherever possible.

Conclusion

The UNICEF Mixed-Methods Impact Evaluation Consultant – Adolescent Girls & Violence Against Children consultancy offers an opportunity for an experienced evaluation professional to contribute to evidence generation on some of the most important challenges affecting children and adolescent girls.

Through the UNICEF Evaluation Office, the consultant will support impact evaluation activities connected to child marriage and social norms, violence prevention in and around schools, and the Power4Girls portfolio focused on girls’ agency, health and wellbeing. The work will also contribute to the broader development and scoping of impact evaluations involving adolescent girls, violence and child protection.

The position requires a strong combination of academic qualifications, professional impact evaluation experience, quantitative and qualitative research expertise, knowledge of violence against children, ethical research capabilities and strong communication skills. Familiarity with statistical and qualitative analysis software, relevant peer-reviewed publications and experience working in low-income settings are also important.

The consultancy is for 12 months, is primarily remote, and may involve travel to project locations. Interested and qualified professionals should prepare their UNICEF TMS profile, CV, cover letter and financial proposal carefully and submit their applications before the 13 September 2026 deadline.

Applicants should also review the complete Terms of Reference and ensure that every required document is submitted in the correct format.

item.content:encoded:
GovAI is inviting applications for a Research Manager (UK Fellowships) position within its Talent Development team. The role offers an opportunity for an experienced professional to help design, select, manage, and deliver GovAI’s UK Seasonal Fellowships while coaching talented individuals pursuing impactful careers in artificial intelligence governance and policy.

The position is particularly suited to someone with excellent project management abilities, strong interpersonal and communication skills, a coaching mindset, professional judgement, and a strong interest in developing talent in the field of AI governance.

The successful candidate will play a significant role in shaping future cohorts of AI governance professionals. Their responsibilities will extend beyond managing fellows to include selection, programme design, events, workshops, stakeholder engagement, programme evaluation, and continuous improvement.

GovAI is also open to candidates who show strong potential but are not yet ready to take on the full responsibilities of Research Manager. Such applicants may be considered for a Research Management Associate role as an initial position.

The application deadline is Sunday, 27 September 2026, at 11:59 PM BST.

About GovAI

GovAI was founded with the mission of helping humanity navigate the transition to a world with advanced artificial intelligence.

The organisation conducts research and works to provide knowledge and assistance to decision-makers across government, industry, and civil society. Its research agenda, first published in 2018, helped contribute to the development of the emerging field of AI governance.

GovAI researchers have published research in prominent academic journals and conferences, including:

  • Science
  • Nature
  • NeurIPS
  • FAccT
  • ICML

The organisation’s researchers and staff have also contributed commentary to influential publications and policy outlets such as TIME, Foreign Affairs, War on the Rocks, and Lawfare.

GovAI’s work has received coverage from major media organisations including The New York Times, Vox, and the Financial Times.

The organisation has staff working across the:

  • United Kingdom
  • United States
  • European Union

One of GovAI’s major approaches to advancing its mission is developing the next generation of talent working on AI governance and policy. The Talent Development team leads these efforts, and the Research Manager position is part of this team.

About the GovAI Seasonal Fellowships

The Research Manager will be closely involved in GovAI’s flagship Seasonal Fellowship programme.

Seasonal Fellowships are three-month opportunities designed to help launch or accelerate impactful careers in AI governance and policy.

GovAI runs two fellowship programmes each year from its London office. Each cohort typically brings together approximately 40 to 50 fellows.

The programme is highly competitive. GovAI reports receiving nearly 20,000 applications each year for approximately 100 places, resulting in an acceptance rate of only around 0.5%.

The fellowship attracts applicants and participants from a remarkably broad range of backgrounds.

While GovAI aims to admit a substantial number of early-career individuals, previous cohorts have also included:

  • Senior government officials
  • Senior academics
  • Software engineers
  • Lawyers
  • Journalists
  • Accomplished professionals from other sectors
  • A New York Times bestselling author
  • A Nobel Peace Prize nominee

This diversity means that the Research Manager will have the opportunity to work with fellows at very different stages of their careers and with a wide range of professional and academic experiences.

What Do Seasonal Fellows Do?

During the fellowship, participants work on projects of their choice.

There are two primary tracks:

Research Track

Fellows on the Research Track conduct a research project related to AI governance or an appropriate area of interest.

Applied Track

Fellows on the Applied Track work on projects outside traditional academic research.

Each fellow is paired with a supervisor drawn from the GovAI team or its wider network.

During the first two weeks, fellows explore the project or projects that would be most valuable for them to pursue. This process involves input from:

  • Their supervisor
  • Their Research Manager
  • The wider GovAI community

The remaining ten weeks are focused on executing the selected projects.

However, the fellowship is not solely about completing an individual project. Fellows also spend time developing their knowledge and skills in AI governance while building professional networks.

GovAI organises activities such as:

  • Q&A sessions with AI governance experts
  • Weekly seminars
  • Skills-development workshops
  • Work-in-progress meetings
  • Peer feedback sessions
  • Social events
  • Career discussions and networking opportunities

Fellows are also encouraged to explore follow-on career opportunities through GovAI’s team and professional network.

Impact of the Seasonal Fellowship

The programme has a strong emphasis on long-term career development.

GovAI reports that approximately 90% of fellows say they are very likely to recommend the fellowship to friends or colleagues.

Participants have also reported that the programme was substantially more valuable to their long-term careers than the alternative activities they would otherwise have pursued.

In its most recent alumni survey, respondents reported that their time at GovAI increased the impact they expect to have in AI governance by approximately 40%.

The Research Manager will therefore have a direct role in helping fellows maximise the long-term value of their fellowship experience.

Why Consider the Research Manager Role?

This position offers the successful candidate the opportunity to combine programme management, talent development, coaching, research, recruitment, events, and strategic decision-making.

1. Help Accelerate Important Careers

A Research Manager will coach approximately 10 to 15 fellows per cohort.

These fellows may range from recent graduates and early-career professionals to highly experienced individuals, including senior government officials.

The manager will help fellows:

  • Define meaningful project goals
  • Develop realistic timelines
  • Overcome challenges
  • Execute ambitious projects
  • Improve their professional skills
  • Navigate career transitions
  • Identify future career opportunities
  • Remain accountable for their objectives

For someone passionate about developing people and helping talented professionals enter or advance in AI governance, this is a central attraction of the role.

2. Help Shape the Future AI Governance Talent Pipeline

The Research Manager will participate in the selection of fellowship cohorts.

Because GovAI receives approximately 20,000 applications annually for around 100 fellowship places, the selection process is extremely competitive.

The successful candidate will therefore contribute directly to decisions about which candidates receive the opportunity to enter the programme.

This responsibility can include:

  • Grading applications
  • Conducting interviews
  • Recommending candidates
  • Participating in decision-making meetings
  • Helping improve the selection process
  • Potentially contributing to fellowship outreach
  • Attending or organising promotional events

This makes the position more than a conventional programme-management role. The Research Manager will help determine which individuals receive opportunities to develop careers in the AI governance field.

3. Grow With a Rapidly Developing Organisation

GovAI describes itself as a rapidly growing organisation with funding in place to continue expanding.

As the organisation develops, the Research Manager is expected to have opportunities to take on additional responsibilities.

The position is therefore intended to provide room for the successful candidate to develop the role according to their:

  • Interests
  • Strengths
  • Experience
  • Skills
  • Capacity

This may make the opportunity particularly attractive to candidates who want a role with significant responsibility and potential for professional growth.

Research Manager Responsibilities

The Research Manager will have a broad set of responsibilities covering fellowship management, recruitment, programme design, events, evaluation, and talent development.

1. Manage Seasonal Fellows

One of the most important responsibilities will be research managing approximately 10 to 15 fellows per cohort.

This involves meeting with each fellow weekly.

The Research Manager will have primary responsibility for making sure fellows:

  • Set clear goals
  • Establish realistic timelines
  • Receive appropriate support
  • Make progress on their projects
  • Address obstacles effectively
  • Successfully navigate their career searches

The Research Manager will also communicate with each fellow’s supervisor.

Supervisors have primary responsibility for providing feedback on fellows’ work, while the Research Manager focuses more broadly on ensuring that the fellowship experience remains productive and that fellows receive the support they need.

2. Participate in Fellowship Selection

The Research Manager will contribute to selecting future fellowship cohorts.

This includes reviewing applications and helping identify candidates who have the potential to make significant contributions to AI governance.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Grading applications
  • Conducting candidate interviews
  • Making candidate recommendations
  • Participating in selection decisions
  • Helping design or improve the selection process

The role may also involve supporting outreach activities intended to attract strong applicants.

The Research Manager may attend or organise events designed to promote the fellowship and communicate opportunities to potential applicants.

3. Help Set Up Each Fellowship

Before each fellowship begins, the Research Manager will contribute to programme preparation.

This can include:

  • Soliciting project suggestions from GovAI’s team and network
  • Recruiting fellowship supervisors
  • Pairing supervisors with incoming fellows
  • Engaging guest speakers
  • Arranging events
  • Developing seminar materials
  • Developing workshop materials
  • Preparing educational and pedagogical resources

This means the role requires strong planning and coordination skills because many programme components need to be prepared before fellows arrive.

4. Run the Day-to-Day Fellowship Programme

The Research Manager will also contribute to the everyday operation of the fellowship.

Responsibilities can include:

  • Running events
  • Organising workshops
  • Moderating expert Q&A sessions
  • Facilitating discussions
  • Hosting fellowship guests
  • Supporting fellows throughout the programme
  • Ensuring a positive and productive participant experience

The successful candidate will therefore need to be comfortable taking responsibility in front of groups and interacting with people from a variety of professional backgrounds.

5. Evaluate Programme Impact

The Research Manager will contribute to assessing the impact of the fellowship programme.

This involves helping GovAI understand whether the programme is achieving its intended outcomes and identifying opportunities for improvement.

Programme evaluation can help determine:

  • What is working effectively
  • Where fellows need additional support
  • Which programme activities create the greatest value
  • How the fellowship affects participants’ careers
  • What changes could improve future cohorts

6. Improve the Fellowship Programme

The Research Manager will be expected to identify and implement changes that could increase the fellowship’s impact.

This requires someone who can:

  • Identify weaknesses
  • Analyse programme outcomes
  • Develop practical improvements
  • Communicate recommendations
  • Implement changes
  • Evaluate whether those changes work

The position therefore combines operational execution with strategic thinking.

Additional Talent Development Responsibilities

Beyond the Seasonal Fellowship itself, the successful candidate may contribute to other aspects of GovAI’s talent development work depending on their skills, interests, experience, and capacity.

Potential responsibilities include:

Talent Database Management

The Research Manager may contribute to managing GovAI’s talent databases.

This can involve maintaining information about individuals in the AI governance ecosystem and helping ensure that relevant talent information remains organised and useful.

External Career Recommendations

The role may also involve providing candidate recommendations for external opportunities when requested.

This could require the Research Manager to understand the skills and career interests of people within GovAI’s network and identify potentially suitable opportunities.

Alumni Career Support

The Research Manager may provide ongoing career support to fellowship alumni after their formal fellowship has ended.

This extends the role beyond the three-month fellowship and allows the Research Manager to contribute to longer-term talent development.

Selection Criteria

GovAI is looking for candidates who combine strong operational skills with interpersonal ability, professional judgement, and a commitment to its mission.

The organisation identifies several core selection criteria.

1. Impact Motivation

Candidates should be genuinely excited by GovAI’s mission.

The successful applicant should want to contribute to making the fellowship programme as effective and impactful as possible.

A strong candidate will therefore be able to demonstrate why AI governance and talent development matter to them and why they want to contribute to GovAI’s work.

2. Excellent Project Management Skills

Strong project management ability is essential.

The Research Manager will need to manage multiple complex workstreams simultaneously.

This requires:

  • Structured working habits
  • Strong organisation
  • Effective prioritisation
  • Attention to detail
  • Reliable execution
  • Ability to manage deadlines
  • Ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders

Candidates should be comfortable working on several priorities at the same time without losing track of important details.

3. Strong Interpersonal Skills and a Coaching Mindset

The position involves working closely with fellows who may be facing challenges in their projects or careers.

The Research Manager needs to be able to provide support while also holding fellows accountable.

This requires a balance between:

  • Empathy
  • Encouragement
  • Constructive feedback
  • Accountability
  • Clear expectations
  • Problem-solving

A coaching mindset is therefore an important part of the position.

4. Professional Judgement and Communication

The Research Manager will represent GovAI to a variety of stakeholders.

These can include:

  • Fellows
  • Internal supervisors
  • External supervisors
  • Fellowship guests
  • Researchers
  • Professionals
  • Other members of GovAI’s network

Candidates must therefore be able to communicate clearly and professionally with people from different backgrounds and at different levels of seniority.

Strong judgement will also be important because the role involves making decisions that affect fellows, programme activities, and selection processes.

5. Drive for Excellence

GovAI is looking for people who are committed to continuously improving themselves.

Candidates should demonstrate:

  • High standards
  • Willingness to learn
  • Receptiveness to feedback
  • Commitment to self-improvement
  • Desire to produce excellent work

The organisation specifically identifies feedback and self-improvement as important components of its culture.

6. Research Experience

Research experience is preferred but not required.

This is because the Research Manager may need to provide feedback on fellows’ research plans and outputs.

Candidates with research experience may therefore have an advantage, particularly if they can demonstrate the ability to assess research questions, methodologies, project plans, and written outputs.

However, applicants should not assume they are ineligible simply because they do not have a traditional research background.

7. Facilitation and Hosting Experience

Experience facilitating or hosting is also preferred but not required.

The Research Manager will be expected to run:

  • Seminars
  • Workshops
  • Expert Q&A sessions
  • Discussion sessions
  • Events involving fellowship guests

Candidates who have experience facilitating professional events, training sessions, workshops, conferences, seminars, or group discussions may therefore find this aspect of the role particularly relevant.

Research Management Associate Alternative

GovAI recognises that some promising applicants may not yet be ready to take on the entire scope of the Research Manager position.

For these candidates, the organisation may consider offering a Research Management Associate role first.

This provides an alternative pathway for strong candidates who demonstrate potential but may need additional experience before assuming full Research Manager responsibilities.

Therefore, candidates should not necessarily rule themselves out solely because they do not meet every aspect of the Research Manager profile.

Salary and Compensation

The position is full-time.

GovAI expects successful candidates to receive annual compensation in the range of:

£83,000 to £105,000 per year

The organisation notes that there may be some flexibility in compensation in situations where salary considerations would otherwise prevent a strong candidate from accepting an offer.

Candidates with specific questions or concerns about compensation or benefits can contact GovAI’s recruitment team.

Employee Benefits

In addition to salary, GovAI lists a range of benefits for the position.

These include:

  • Health insurance
  • Dental insurance
  • Vision insurance
  • 10% employer pension contribution
  • £5,000 annual wellbeing budget
  • £5,000 annual professional development budget
  • £5,000 annual childcare budget
  • £1,800 annual commuting allowance
  • Flexible working hours
  • Extended parental leave
  • 33 days of annual leave, including public holidays

The professional development budget may be particularly valuable for a candidate looking to continue building expertise in AI governance, management, research, leadership, or related areas.

Location and Visa Sponsorship

The Research Manager must be based in London, United Kingdom, during fellowship periods.

The fellowship periods are:

  • January to April
  • June to August

Outside fellowship periods, short periods of remote work are possible.

Importantly, GovAI is able to sponsor visas.

This means that candidates who require visa sponsorship to work in the United Kingdom can still be considered for the position.

Applicants who have questions about their circumstances or whether visa-related considerations affect their application should contact GovAI’s recruitment team.

How the Application Process Works

The selection process consists of three main stages.

Stage 1: Written Application

Candidates will first submit a written application.

APPLY HERE

This stage is an opportunity to demonstrate:

  • Motivation for GovAI’s mission
  • Relevant professional experience
  • Project management abilities
  • Communication skills
  • Coaching or mentoring experience
  • Research experience, if applicable
  • Facilitation experience, if applicable
  • Understanding of the role
  • Reasons for wanting to contribute to talent development in AI governance

Applicants should make sure their written responses clearly demonstrate evidence rather than simply listing skills.

Stage 2: Paid Remote Work Test

Candidates who progress beyond the written application will complete a paid remote work test.

This stage is designed to give GovAI an opportunity to assess how candidates approach practical work relevant to the position.

It also gives candidates an opportunity to demonstrate their abilities through actual work rather than relying entirely on application materials.

Stage 3: Interviews and Reference Checks

The final stage involves interviews and reference checks.

Successful candidates will therefore need to be prepared to discuss their experience, judgement, communication style, motivation, and ability to perform the responsibilities of the role.

For more information visit the GOVAI website HERE

More fellowship programs visit the OFY Website HERE

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the GovAI Research Manager (UK Fellowships) position is:

Sunday, 27 September 2026, at 11:59 PM BST.

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

Candidates who require a decision by a particular date are encouraged to contact GovAI’s recruitment team.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity could be particularly suitable for professionals who enjoy combining people management, programme delivery, research, career development, and strategic planning.

Potentially relevant candidates include:

  • Project managers
  • Programme managers
  • Research managers
  • Research programme coordinators
  • Talent development professionals
  • Fellowship managers
  • Academic programme managers
  • Policy professionals
  • AI governance professionals
  • Researchers
  • Consultants
  • Government professionals
  • Professionals with strong coaching or mentoring experience
  • Professionals experienced in organising workshops and seminars
  • Professionals experienced in managing complex multi-stakeholder projects

The vacancy does not state a specific degree requirement or restrict applications to a particular nationality, country, race, or continent.

GovAI specifically says it welcomes applicants from a wide range of backgrounds and encourages people to apply even if their experience does not align perfectly with every qualification.

This is important for candidates who have transferable experience but may not have previously held the exact title of Research Manager.

What Makes This Opportunity Stand Out?

Several aspects make this position particularly notable.

High Level of Responsibility

The successful candidate will have significant responsibility for managing fellows, contributing to selection decisions, organising programme activities, and improving the fellowship.

Strong Compensation

The expected annual compensation of £83,000–£105,000 places the position at a highly competitive salary level.

Visa Sponsorship

GovAI can sponsor visas, potentially making the opportunity accessible to qualified international applicants who require UK work authorisation.

Professional Development

The role includes a £5,000 annual professional development budget, allowing the successful candidate to invest in their continued growth.

Wellbeing Support

The position includes a £5,000 annual wellbeing budget.

Career Impact

The Research Manager will directly support professionals seeking to build careers in AI governance and policy, potentially influencing the development of future leaders and researchers in the field.

Exposure to a Diverse Talent Network

Because GovAI’s fellows come from government, academia, technology, journalism, law, research, and other professional backgrounds, the position offers significant exposure to a broad network of talented individuals.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Candidates interested in applying should carefully demonstrate how their previous experience connects to the responsibilities of the role.

A strong application could highlight examples of:

  1. Managing complex projects: Explain situations where you managed multiple deadlines, stakeholders, deliverables, or workstreams.
  2. Coaching or mentoring people: Demonstrate how you have helped others set goals, overcome challenges, improve performance, or advance professionally.
  3. Programme coordination: Highlight experience organising programmes, fellowships, training initiatives, conferences, workshops, or similar activities.
  4. Stakeholder management: Provide examples of working effectively with people from different organisations, professional backgrounds, or levels of seniority.
  5. Research and analysis: If you have research experience, explain how you have designed, assessed, conducted, or communicated research.
  6. Facilitation: Highlight experience leading meetings, workshops, seminars, training sessions, panels, or discussions.
  7. Attention to detail: Give evidence of situations where careful planning and execution were critical to success.
  8. Mission alignment: Clearly explain why AI governance and talent development are meaningful to you.
  9. Continuous improvement: Show examples of receiving feedback, learning from it, and improving your work.
  10. Career judgement: Demonstrate situations where you had to make thoughtful decisions with incomplete information or competing priorities.

Important Information for Applicants

Before applying, candidates should take note of the following:

  • The role is full-time.
  • The position is based in London, UK during fellowship periods.
  • Fellowship periods are January–April and June–August.
  • Short periods of remote work may be possible outside fellowship periods.
  • GovAI can sponsor visas.
  • Expected annual compensation is £83,000–£105,000.
  • Research experience is preferred but not required.
  • Facilitation and hosting experience is preferred but not required.
  • Strong project management and interpersonal skills are central requirements.
  • Candidates who are not yet ready for the full Research Manager role may be considered for a Research Management Associate position.
  • The recruitment process includes a written application, paid remote work test, interviews, and reference checks.
  • The application deadline is Sunday, 27 September 2026, at 11:59 PM BST.

Conclusion

The GovAI Research Manager (UK Fellowships) position is a significant opportunity for an experienced professional who wants to combine project management, talent development, coaching, research, programme design, and AI governance.

The successful candidate will not simply administer a fellowship. They will help shape the experience of highly promising professionals, participate in decisions about who enters GovAI’s talent-development pipeline, support fellows through ambitious projects and career transitions, organise educational activities, engage with experts and supervisors, and contribute to improving one of GovAI’s flagship programmes.

With expected compensation of £83,000 to £105,000 per year, extensive employee benefits, professional development support, the possibility of visa sponsorship, and the opportunity to work with a highly selective international talent programme, the position could be particularly attractive to professionals seeking a high-impact career in AI governance and talent development.

Applicants should carefully review their experience against the selection criteria and clearly demonstrate evidence of project management, interpersonal skills, professional judgement, communication, coaching ability, and commitment to excellence.

Importantly, GovAI encourages applications from a broad range of backgrounds and notes that candidates do not need to match every qualification perfectly. Individuals who are promising but not yet ready for the full Research Manager position may also be considered for the Research Management Associate pathway.

Interested candidates should ensure that their applications are submitted by Sunday, 27 September 2026, at 11:59 PM BST.
