item.content:encoded:
The Equity | Impact Center (EIC) is a research-based capacity-building organization working across sectors to strengthen artists, leaders, founders, organizations and ecosystems while advancing equity and improving the quality of life for marginalized communities in the Pittsburgh Region and throughout the United States.

Founded in 2022, the Equity | Impact Center focuses on organizational capacity building, leadership development, entrepreneurial advancement and collective impact. Its work combines research, data, expertise and lived experience to develop programs and solutions designed to create meaningful and sustainable change.

About the Equity | Impact Center

The Equity | Impact Center was established with a vision of creating a community-centered organization capable of identifying and addressing gaps through research, data collection, data analysis, comprehensive program design and collaboration.

The organization works across sectors to empower people and organizations developing solutions to social challenges.

Its approach is based on the belief that transformative results can be achieved when programs and solutions combine:

  • Proven frameworks and methodologies
  • Accurate data
  • Relevant skills and knowledge
  • Professional expertise
  • Insights from people with lived experience
  • Thoughtful collaboration

Through this approach, EIC seeks to strengthen its stakeholders and contribute to positive outcomes across the Pittsburgh Region and beyond.

What the Equity | Impact Center Does

The Equity | Impact Center develops transformative programs and comprehensive strategic solutions focused on strengthening the capacity of individuals, organizations and ecosystems.

Its work includes:

  • Organizational capacity building
  • Leadership development
  • Entrepreneurial advancement
  • Fellowship initiatives
  • Ecosystem development
  • Collective impact
  • Strategic collaboration
  • Research and data analysis
  • Program design
  • Support for artists and founders

The organization seeks to empower solutions that are informed by both professional expertise and lived experience.

Programs and Initiatives

The Equity | Impact Center highlights fellowship and ecosystem initiatives designed to support artists, founders and leaders across sectors.

These initiatives form part of a broader strategy to strengthen individuals while improving the systems and environments in which they operate.

The organization’s programmes and services are intended to support people and organizations whose ability to create social impact depends on strong internal capacity and coordinated systems.

Interested individuals and organizations should review the specific programme information provided by EIC because eligibility requirements, application processes and availability may differ between initiatives.

Who the Equity | Impact Center Works With

EIC focuses on leaders, organizations and institutions working to create social impact.

Nonprofit and Social Impact Leaders

The organization works with nonprofit and social impact leaders and organizations that are advancing equity.

Its capacity-building approach helps these organizations strengthen their internal systems and ability to deliver sustainable impact.

Institutions and Funders

EIC also works with institutions and funders that are committed to sustainable, systems-level impact.

These partnerships support coordinated approaches to addressing complex challenges and advancing equity.

Founders and Artists

Founders and artists seeking to develop viable solutions and establish sustainable careers are another important group served by the organization.

EIC’s work recognizes the importance of supporting creative and entrepreneurial leaders whose ideas and lived experiences can contribute to broader social change.

Grounded in Research, Data, Expertise and Lived Experience

Research and evidence are central to the Equity | Impact Center’s approach.

Since its launch in 2022, the organization has sought to bridge identified gaps through:

  1. Research
  2. Data collection
  3. Data analysis
  4. Comprehensive programme design
  5. Thoughtful collaboration

The organization combines these approaches with the knowledge and perspectives of people who have direct lived experience of the issues being addressed.

This allows EIC to support solutions that are informed by both evidence and the realities experienced by communities.

Organizational Capacity Building

A major focus of the Equity | Impact Center is helping organizations develop the capacity needed to achieve sustainable impact.

This includes strengthening organizational systems and leadership capabilities for equity-centered work.

The organization recognizes that effective social impact requires more than individual leadership. Strong internal organizational capacity and coordinated systems are also important to achieving long-term results.

Leadership Development

EIC’s work includes developing leadership acumen for equity-centered initiatives.

Through its programs and partnerships, the organization seeks to empower leaders with resources, knowledge, skills and networks that can help them advance their work.

Leadership development is connected to EIC’s broader mission of creating a more equitable and just future.

Entrepreneurial Advancement

The Equity | Impact Center supports founders and entrepreneurs seeking to build viable solutions and sustainable careers.

Its approach recognizes that founders can play an important role in developing innovative responses to social challenges.

By combining entrepreneurial advancement with equity-centered capacity building, EIC seeks to help founders strengthen their ability to develop and sustain their work.

Collective Impact and Ecosystem Development

EIC also works at the ecosystem level.

Rather than focusing exclusively on individual participants or organizations, its work considers the relationships and systems that influence social impact.

Partnerships among nonprofits, institutions, funders, founders, artists and other stakeholders can help create coordinated approaches to complex challenges.

The Five Values Guiding EIC’s Work

The Equity | Impact Center identifies five values that guide its programs, partnerships and decision-making.

1. Advance

EIC provides resources and empowers leaders with the intention of contributing to a more equitable and just future.

2. Amplify

The organization strengthens the voices and empowers the ideas of programme participants.

3. Authenticity

EIC recognizes the combined value of lived experience, knowledge and expertise.

4. Access

The organization seeks to ensure that resources and networks are available to underserved and marginalized people.

5. Accountability

EIC aims to incorporate its equity-centered value system throughout planning, decision-making, implementation and evaluation.

Who May Benefit From EIC Programs?

Based on the organization’s stated areas of work, its programs and initiatives may be relevant to:

  • Nonprofit leaders
  • Social impact organizations
  • Equity-focused organizations
  • Founders
  • Entrepreneurs
  • Artists
  • Community leaders
  • Institutions
  • Funders
  • Ecosystem partners

However, the provided source does not establish one universal eligibility requirement for all EIC programs. Specific qualifications, application requirements and deadlines should be confirmed on the individual programme page.

Explore Equity | Impact Center Programs

Individuals and organizations interested in EIC’s work can explore its available programs and services through the organization’s official programmes page.

The organization also provides opportunities for institutions and other stakeholders interested in partnering with EIC.

Because the source does not identify a single specific open fellowship, scholarship, grant or job, applicants should review the individual programme details before assuming that an initiative is currently accepting applications.

Impact and Continued Growth

The Equity | Impact Center describes itself as having developed into a community asset supporting organizational capacity building, entrepreneurial advancement, collective impact and leadership development.

Its initiatives operate across sectors and are designed to empower solutions developed through a combination of lived experience, critical skills, knowledge, expertise and innovative perspectives.

The organization also provides an impact report documenting its work and development.

Conclusion

The Equity | Impact Center is a research-based capacity-building organization focused on strengthening people, organizations and ecosystems working to advance equity.

Its work brings together research, data, professional expertise, lived experience and collaboration to support organizational capacity building, leadership development, entrepreneurial advancement and collective impact.

Through its programs, fellowship and ecosystem initiatives, EIC works with nonprofit and social impact leaders, institutions, funders, founders and artists seeking to create sustainable solutions and careers.

Individuals and organizations interested in participating should explore the Equity | Impact Center’s current programs and services and review the specific requirements of each initiative.

item.content:encoded:
The Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships and Mentorships 2027 are inviting photographers and visual storytellers from around the world to develop long-term documentary photography projects focused on environmental and conservation challenges.

The programme is designed to support photographers who use visual storytelling to explore environmental issues while highlighting the people, communities and organizations working to protect the planet, wildlife and natural habitats.

In 2027, Vital Impacts plans to award one $20,000 fellowship to an established environmental photographer, six $5,000 fellowships to emerging photographers from around the world, and ten mentorships for photographers whose work demonstrates strong potential and would benefit from additional professional guidance.

The programme emphasizes long-term documentary storytelling, meaningful relationships with communities and ethical approaches to photography. Prior publication experience is not required.

About Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships

Vital Impacts is a nonprofit organization that uses journalism and visual storytelling to amplify the work of communities protecting people, wildlife and habitats around the world.

Its Environmental Photography Fellowships and Mentorships provide financial support, mentorship and creative independence to photographers developing significant bodies of work around environmental and conservation issues.

The programme is particularly interested in projects that move beyond simply documenting environmental problems. Applicants are encouraged to tell stories about the people, communities and initiatives developing solutions to environmental and conservation challenges.

Each fellowship supports one photographer and one documentary project during the fellowship and mentorship period. Recipients receive time, financial support and guidance from the Vital Impacts mentorship community while developing their proposed project.

At the end of the programme, recipients are expected to have made meaningful progress on their proposed project and developed a substantial body of work that could be suitable for publication, exhibition or other forms of public engagement.

Vital Impacts Photography Fellowships 2027 Awards

For 2027, the programme will provide three categories of support:

One $20,000 Fellowship

One $20,000 fellowship will be awarded to an established environmental photographer.

Six $5,000 Fellowships

Six $5,000 fellowships will be awarded to emerging photographers from around the world.

Ten Mentorships

Ten photographers will receive mentorship support. These applicants should demonstrate strong potential and have work that would benefit from additional guidance and professional support.

The combination of financial support and mentorship is intended to give photographers the opportunity to spend significant time developing their projects and producing thoughtful, deeply reported visual stories.

New Exhibition Opportunity in Italy

Vital Impacts has expanded its partnership with the Festival of Ethical Photography to create an additional opportunity for one of the seven fellowship recipients.

One fellowship recipient will be selected at a later stage to exhibit their work at the 2027 Festival of Ethical Photography in Lodi, Italy.

The selected photographer will benefit from the Festival’s international platform for documentary photography and photojournalism focused on important social and environmental issues.

The Festival will cover:

  • The full costs of producing the exhibition.
  • Installation costs.
  • International travel for the selected photographer.
  • Accommodation to attend the Festival.
  • The opportunity to present the work in person.

This partnership can provide the selected fellow with an opportunity to reach an international audience and connect with photographers, editors, conservationists and members of the public interested in environmental and social issues.

Who Should Apply?

Vital Impacts is particularly interested in photographers who have developed meaningful and established relationships with the people, places and issues they document.

The programme places strong emphasis on photographers who take time to:

  • Listen to communities.
  • Build trust.
  • Understand local context.
  • Develop meaningful relationships.
  • Return to stories over time.
  • Produce long-term documentary work.

Vital Impacts strongly encourages applications from photographers documenting environmental and conservation stories within their own communities.

Local photographers can bring knowledge, access, relationships and perspectives that may provide greater depth and authenticity to the stories being documented.

However, applicants do not necessarily need to live permanently in the location they propose to document.

The programme will also consider photographers who can demonstrate sustained knowledge and engagement through:

  • Recurring travel.
  • Long-term collaborations.
  • Professional experience.
  • Academic experience.
  • Other meaningful relationships with the community or issue.

Applicants should clearly explain why they are the right person to tell their proposed story, including what they know, who they know, what relationships they have developed and what unique perspective they bring.

What Does Vital Impacts Look For?

Successful applications should demonstrate the ability to communicate the complexity of environmental and conservation challenges while also showing potential solutions.

Vital Impacts is looking for photographers who can demonstrate:

Meaningful Relationships

Applicants should have a meaningful and sustained relationship with the community, environmental issue or conservation initiative they intend to document.

Understanding of the Issue

Applicants should demonstrate a clear understanding of the environmental issue and explain its wider significance.

A Realistic Project Plan

Applicants should present a thoughtful and realistic plan for developing the project over a 12-month period.

Existing Access and Trust

Where appropriate, applicants should demonstrate existing access to the community or issue and evidence of established trust.

Ethical Storytelling

Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to ethical and responsible storytelling.

Strong Photography

Applications should demonstrate distinctive visual approaches and strong photographic ability.

Public Impact

The proposed project should have potential to contribute meaningfully to public understanding of environmental and conservation issues.

Is Previous Publication Experience Required?

No.

Prior publication experience is specifically stated as not being a requirement for applicants.

This means photographers should focus on demonstrating the strength of their visual work, their relationship with the proposed subject or community, their understanding of the issue and their ability to develop a meaningful long-term documentary project.

Ethical Storytelling Requirements

Ethics are an important part of the Vital Impacts programme.

All winners are required to comply with the Vital Impacts Code of Ethics throughout the application, fellowship or mentorship, production and delivery of their project.

Applicants are expected to review the Code of Ethics before applying and agree to comply with it if selected.

Vital Impacts may assess ethical compliance through several mechanisms, including:

  • Review of submitted work and project materials.
  • Review of the applicant’s project statement.
  • Assessment of the applicant’s relationship with the community or issue.
  • Regular check-ins.
  • Communications with mentors and the Vital Impacts team.
  • Review of concerns or complaints.
  • Requests for additional information or clarification.
  • Review of project materials, captions, metadata and other documentation where necessary.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed projects are based on responsible, respectful and ethical documentary practices.

What Will Fellowship Recipients Do?

The fellowship or mentorship period is intended to give recipients the time and support needed to develop a substantial documentary project.

During the programme, recipients will work on their proposed projects while receiving guidance from the Vital Impacts mentorship community.

The expected outcome is meaningful progress toward a substantial body of work that can potentially be:

  • Published.
  • Exhibited.
  • Presented to the public.
  • Used to increase understanding of environmental and conservation issues.

Key Benefits of the Programme

The programme provides different forms of support depending on the award received.

Key opportunities include:

  • A $20,000 fellowship for one established environmental photographer.
  • Six $5,000 fellowships for emerging photographers worldwide.
  • Ten mentorship opportunities.
  • Ongoing guidance from the Vital Impacts mentorship community.
  • Financial support for developing a documentary photography project.
  • Creative independence during project development.
  • An opportunity to develop a substantial long-term body of work.
  • Potential publication, exhibition and public engagement opportunities.
  • A special exhibition opportunity at the 2027 Festival of Ethical Photography in Lodi, Italy for one selected fellowship recipient.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Photographers interested in applying should pay particular attention to the relationship between their proposed story, their existing experience and their ability to access and document the issue responsibly.

1. Choose a Strong Environmental Story

Select an environmental or conservation issue that has clear significance and where there are people, communities or initiatives working toward solutions.

2. Demonstrate Your Relationship to the Story

Explain your existing relationship with the people, community, location or issue.

The programme places considerable emphasis on sustained engagement and trust.

3. Present a Long-Term Approach

Avoid presenting the project as a short-term photography assignment. Explain how the story can develop over the proposed 12-month period.

4. Show Your Visual Strength

Your portfolio and proposed project should demonstrate a distinctive visual approach and strong photographic ability.

5. Explain Your Ethical Approach

Show that you understand the responsibilities involved in documenting people and communities and that you are prepared to follow the Vital Impacts Code of Ethics.

6. Focus on Solutions

While environmental challenges are important, Vital Impacts specifically seeks stories that also illuminate the people and initiatives working toward solutions.

7. Explain the Potential Impact

Describe how the completed project could help audiences better understand the environmental or conservation issue.

Application Timeline

The programme page currently indicates that the opportunity is open for submissions. Applicants should consult the official application page for the exact submission timeline and current closing date before applying.

Applications are hosted through Picter, which provides the submission platform for the Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowship 2027.

How to Apply

Interested photographers should first review the programme information, timeline, FAQ and terms before starting their submission.

Applicants can access the official submission platform and begin their application through the Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowship 2027 application page.

The programme page provides a “Start submission” option for applicants.

Applicants should also review the Vital Impacts Code of Ethics before submitting.

Conclusion

The Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships and Mentorships 2027 offer photographers an opportunity to develop long-term documentary projects focused on environmental and conservation challenges and the people working to address them.

The programme combines financial support, mentorship and creative independence, with awards ranging from a $20,000 fellowship for an established photographer to six $5,000 fellowships for emerging photographers, alongside ten mentorship opportunities.

The programme is particularly suitable for photographers who have meaningful relationships with the communities or issues they document and who are committed to ethical, long-term storytelling.

Photographers should carefully develop their project concept, demonstrate their connection to the proposed story and explain how their work can contribute to greater public understanding of environmental and conservation issues.

Discover more fellowship opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The Hinrich Foundation has opened its Call for Research Proposals 2026, inviting researchers and research organizations to submit proposals for research projects that advance understanding of global trade issues and contribute to policy development.

Through its international trade research program, the Foundation supports research across a broad range of trade-related sectors. Proposals are particularly encouraged in areas including trade governance, the geopolitics of trade, foreign direct investment, global supply chain resilience and security, digital trade and technology, environmental sustainability, workforce and education, industrial competitiveness, natural resources, and trade logistics and services.

The upcoming submission deadline is October 31, 2026.

About the Hinrich Foundation Research Programme

The Hinrich Foundation is an independent Asia-based philanthropic organization dedicated to advancing mutually beneficial and sustainable global trade.

Its international trade research program seeks to promote research that can strengthen understanding of global trade challenges and support policy development.

Researchers and research organizations are invited to propose projects addressing significant trade-related questions. The Foundation reviews proposals twice each year, following the closing of each submission cycle.

The annual submission deadlines are:

  • May 31
  • October 31

The next opportunity to submit a proposal is October 31, 2026.

Priority Research Areas

The Foundation supports research across several areas of international trade. Its stated priority areas, in order, are:

1. Trade Governance

Research examining trade governance and the systems, institutions and policies that shape international trade.

2. The Geopolitics of Trade

Research exploring the relationship between geopolitics and international trade and the ways political developments influence global trade.

3. Foreign Direct Investment

Research focused on foreign direct investment and its relationship with international trade and economic activity.

4. Global Supply Chain Resilience and Security

Projects examining the resilience and security of global supply chains and issues affecting their reliability and stability.

5. Digital Trade, Innovation and Technology

Research examining digital trade, innovation and technology and their growing influence on international commerce.

6. Trade and Environmental Sustainability

Research investigating the relationship between international trade and environmental sustainability.

7. Trade Workforce and Education

Projects examining workforce and education issues connected to international trade and economic development.

8. Industrial Competitiveness and Economic Development

Research exploring industrial competitiveness and the contribution of trade to economic development.

9. Natural Resources in Trade

Research examining the role of natural resources within international trade.

10. Trade Logistics and Services

Research addressing trade logistics and services that support international commerce.

Who Can Submit a Proposal?

The call invites:

  • Individual researchers
  • Groups of researchers
  • Research organizations

The provided call does not state a specific nationality, citizenship or country requirement for applicants. Researchers and organizations should therefore focus on whether their proposed research fits within the Foundation’s international trade research priorities and meets the submission requirements.

What Should the Research Proposal Include?

The Hinrich Foundation asks researchers to include specific information in their proposals.

1. Name and Credentials of the Researcher or Researchers

Applicants should provide the names and relevant credentials of the researcher or researchers responsible for the proposed project.

This section should help demonstrate the researcher’s expertise and ability to undertake the proposed work.

2. Synopsis of the Proposed Research

The proposal should include a clear synopsis of the research being proposed.

The Foundation encourages researchers to:

  • Address major trade-related themes.
  • Identify the central issue the research will investigate.
  • Present two to four key questions that the research seeks to answer.
  • Explain the proposed research approach.
  • Specify whether the research will use primary or secondary research.

Researchers should make the proposed research questions clear and demonstrate how the project will contribute to understanding an important trade issue.

Research Format and Publication

The Hinrich Foundation generally publishes research in two formats:

  • White papers: Approximately 4,000 words
  • Articles: Approximately 1,600 words

All research products will be subject to the Foundation’s editorial review.

Researchers may propose either a new research project or an overview or summary of existing work.

New Research Project

A researcher may propose a new research project that includes any combination of article and/or white paper deliverables.

Existing Research

Researchers may also propose an overview or summary of existing work, including research that has already been published elsewhere.

It is important to note that the final decision to publish research rests entirely with the Foundation.

Deliverable Timetable

The Foundation encourages research projects to be completed within four months from the point of commission.

During the project, the researcher should provide updates to the Foundation at mutually agreed regular intervals.

Researchers are also encouraged to consider feedback from the Foundation’s research program team regarding the progress and findings of the project.

In some cases, researchers may be asked to produce one or two interim articles of approximately 1,600 words before completing the full research project. These interim articles may summarize findings from the research that is still underway.

Funding Request

Funding for successful research projects is negotiable.

The Foundation may provide full or partial financial support for successful proposals.

Funding is typically paid at the point of completion of the project.

Researchers should therefore clearly communicate their funding requirements when submitting their proposal.

How to Prepare a Strong Proposal

Researchers interested in submitting should ensure that their proposal clearly explains the proposed research and its relevance to global trade.

A strong submission should:

  1. Clearly identify the researcher or research team.
  2. Provide relevant credentials and expertise.
  3. Explain the proposed research topic.
  4. Identify two to four key research questions.
  5. Explain whether the research will use primary or secondary research.
  6. Identify the expected research outputs.
  7. Provide a realistic project timetable.
  8. Clearly state the requested funding.
  9. Demonstrate relevance to one or more of the Foundation’s priority research areas.

How to Apply

Researchers and research organizations interested in the call should first review the Hinrich Foundation application guidelines and then submit their research proposal through the designated submission form.

The Foundation has provided a dedicated submission process for researchers to submit their proposals.

Upcoming submission deadline: October 31, 2026

Applicants should ensure that their proposals are completed and submitted before the deadline.

Important Considerations

The Foundation’s call states that successful proposals may receive full or partial financial support. However, funding is negotiable and is typically paid upon completion of the project.

Researchers should also be aware that receiving support does not automatically mean that a research product will be published. All research products are subject to editorial review, and the Foundation retains the final decision regarding publication.

Conclusion

The Hinrich Foundation Call for Research Proposals 2026 offers researchers and research organizations an opportunity to develop research addressing important global trade issues and contributing to policy development.

The programme covers a wide range of subjects, including trade governance, trade geopolitics, foreign direct investment, supply chain resilience, digital trade, environmental sustainability, workforce and education, economic development, natural resources, and logistics.

Researchers with relevant expertise are encouraged to develop clear research questions, explain their methodology, outline their proposed deliverables and identify their funding requirements.

The next submission deadline is October 31, 2026.

Interested researchers should review the application guidelines and submit their proposals through the official submission form before the deadline.

Discover more on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The Social Science Research Council (SSRC), through its African Peacebuilding and Developmental Dynamics (APDD) program, is inviting applications for the Individual Research Fellowship (IRF). The fellowship is designed to support African researchers, policy analysts, and practitioners whose work focuses on conflict, peacebuilding, governance, and developmental dynamics across the African continent.

In 2026, the program plans to award up to nine individual research fellowships, with each fellowship providing a maximum award of $12,000.

The Individual Research Fellowship is intended to strengthen the quality, visibility, and impact of independent African peacebuilding research. It provides fellows with an opportunity to undertake field-based research, analyze and communicate their findings, participate in professional workshops, receive mentorship, build networks with other African scholars and practitioners, and contribute to important conversations around peacebuilding policy and practice.

The fellowship is particularly valuable for professionals seeking to ensure that African perspectives and evidence-based research play a stronger role in regional and global discussions concerning peace, governance, development, and conflict transformation.

About the African Peacebuilding and Developmental Dynamics Program

The African Peacebuilding and Developmental Dynamics (APDD) program is part of the Social Science Research Council’s work to strengthen social science research and make research-based knowledge more accessible to policymakers, practitioners, researchers, and other stakeholders.

Since its establishment in 2012, the Individual Research Fellowship has served as a mechanism for improving the quality and visibility of independent African peacebuilding research both within Africa and internationally.

The program also seeks to bridge the gap between research, policy, and practice. Rather than limiting research to academic audiences, the fellowship encourages fellows to produce knowledge that can be used by policymakers, practitioners, research institutions, civil society organizations, and other peacebuilding constituencies.

Through the program, fellows are expected to contribute evidence and African perspectives to regional and global debates concerning peacebuilding.

Individual Research Fellowship 2026 at a Glance

The major details of the fellowship include:

  • Program: African Peacebuilding and Developmental Dynamics (APDD)
  • Fellowship: Individual Research Fellowship (IRF)
  • Host organization: Social Science Research Council (SSRC)
  • Number of awards: Up to nine fellowships
  • Maximum fellowship award: $12,000 per fellow
  • Research duration: Six months of field-based research
  • Analysis and writing period: Three months
  • Total fellowship period: Nine months
  • Program period stated: July 2026 to March 2027
  • Target applicants: African researchers, academics, policy analysts, and practitioners
  • Geographic eligibility: African citizens currently residing in an African country
  • Research focus: Conflict, peacebuilding, governance, and developmental dynamics
  • Workshops: Two mandatory APDD workshops
  • Funding: Andrew Carnegie Foundation
  • Application: Online application
  • Application deadline: Not stated in the information provided

What Does the Individual Research Fellowship Offer?

The APDD Individual Research Fellowship goes beyond financial support for research. Fellows become part of a broader professional and intellectual community focused on strengthening African knowledge production and peacebuilding practice.

The program has several major components.

1. Field-Based Research and Thought Leadership

One of the central elements of the fellowship is the opportunity to conduct substantial field-based research.

Fellows commit to:

  • Six months of field-based research; and
  • Three months dedicated to analysis and writing.

This represents a total fellowship period of nine months, running from July 2026 to March 2027, according to the information provided.

The research undertaken through the fellowship is expected to generate knowledge that is relevant to peacebuilding scholarship, policy, and practice in Africa.

The program seeks research that can have a meaningful impact rather than research that remains confined to academic discussions. Fellows are therefore expected to produce evidence-based knowledge capable of contributing to regional and global conversations about peacebuilding.

This provides researchers with an opportunity to examine important peace and conflict-related issues from African perspectives while generating evidence that can potentially inform policy and practice.

2. Mandatory APDD Workshops

Fellows will participate in two mandatory APDD workshops, scheduled to take place in July and January in different regions of Africa.

These workshops are an important part of the fellowship experience because they provide fellows with opportunities to develop both their research and professional capabilities.

During the workshops, fellows can:

  • Refine their research designs.
  • Improve their research focus.
  • Strengthen their research methodologies.
  • Present and discuss research findings.
  • Receive feedback from experienced academics and practitioners.
  • Explore strategies for making their research accessible to broader audiences.
  • Discuss opportunities for publication.
  • Network with other fellows.
  • Develop professional relationships with senior scholars.
  • Engage with practitioners working in peacebuilding.
  • Learn from facilitators with relevant expertise.

The workshops therefore provide an environment where fellows can test their ideas, receive constructive feedback, and strengthen their research before communicating their findings to wider audiences.

3. Contribution to African Scholarship and Knowledge Production

Another major component of the fellowship is knowledge dissemination.

Fellows are expected to contribute to the broader APDD knowledge-production ecosystem. This includes opportunities to contribute to:

  • The APDD Working Paper series.
  • The African Peacebuilding Policy Review and Analysis.
  • APDD digital forums.
  • Kujenga Amani.
  • APDD social media platforms, including Facebook and X.

Fellows may also have opportunities to contribute to external academic and public-facing platforms.

These may include:

  • International peer-reviewed journals.
  • Books.
  • Academic articles.
  • Essays.
  • Blogs.
  • Feature articles.
  • Opinion and editorial articles.
  • Podcasts.

This aspect of the fellowship can be particularly valuable for researchers and practitioners seeking to increase the visibility and accessibility of their work.

Rather than producing research solely for specialist academic audiences, fellows are encouraged to explore different formats and platforms through which their findings can reach policymakers, practitioners, researchers, communities, and the broader public.

4. Professional Development and Career Advancement

The fellowship also provides opportunities for professional development.

Fellows will gain new knowledge and skills that can help advance their careers as academics or practitioners.

For academics, this can provide an opportunity to strengthen their research portfolios, develop publications, expand professional networks, and increase their visibility within African and international peacebuilding scholarship.

For policy analysts and practitioners, the fellowship can provide an opportunity to deepen research capabilities and develop evidence-based approaches to peacebuilding-related work.

The combination of research, workshops, mentorship, publication opportunities, and networking makes the fellowship relevant to professionals interested in building long-term careers around peacebuilding, governance, development, conflict analysis, research, and policy.

5. Networking and Building an African Peacebuilding Community

Fellows become part of a network of active African scholars and practitioners working on peacebuilding.

The program seeks to develop a community capable of bringing African perspectives into global discussions about peacebuilding, conflict, governance, and development.

Through this network, fellows can potentially establish relationships with:

  • Other African researchers.
  • Senior academics.
  • Policy professionals.
  • Peacebuilding practitioners.
  • Research institutions.
  • Regional organizations.
  • Civil society professionals.
  • Other experts working on peace and development issues.

These relationships can provide opportunities for peer learning, collaboration, knowledge exchange, and future research partnerships.

6. Mentorship from Senior Scholars

Fellows will receive mentorship from experienced senior scholars working in the field.

Mentorship is an important component because fellows can benefit from the experience of established researchers while developing their own research and professional careers.

The program also emphasizes peer-to-peer learning, meaning fellows can learn not only from senior experts but also from one another.

This creates an environment where researchers and practitioners working on different peacebuilding issues can exchange perspectives and develop collaborative relationships.

Who Can Apply for the APDD Individual Research Fellowship?

The fellowship is specifically designed for African citizens currently residing in an African country.

The competition is open to African academics as well as policy analysts and practitioners working on relevant peacebuilding issues.

However, eligibility requirements differ depending on whether an applicant is applying as an academic or as a policy analyst/practitioner.

Eligibility Requirements for Academic Applicants

Applicants applying as academics must meet specific educational and professional requirements.

They must:

  1. Be an African citizen.
  2. Currently reside in an African country.
  3. Hold a full-time faculty or research position.
  4. Work at an African university or research organization.
  5. Hold a PhD obtained no earlier than January 2016.

The fellowship therefore targets established researchers who are already professionally connected to an African university or research institution.

PhD Requirement

The fellowship specifies that academic applicants must have obtained their PhD no earlier than January 2016.

The information also states that applicants who had not been awarded their PhDs by June 2026 would not have their cases prioritized for eligibility as academics.

Applicants should therefore carefully review the official application guidance concerning their PhD completion status and eligibility before applying.

Eligibility Requirements for Policy Analysts and Practitioners

The fellowship is also open to African policy analysts and practitioners working in peacebuilding-related fields.

Applicants in this category must:

  • Be African citizens.
  • Currently reside in an African country.
  • Be based in Africa.
  • Work at an eligible regional or sub-regional institution, government agency, nongovernmental organization, media organization, or civil society organization.
  • Hold at least a master’s degree.
  • Have obtained the master’s degree before January 2021.
  • Have at least five years of proven research and work experience in peacebuilding-related activities on the African continent.

This pathway makes the fellowship accessible to experienced professionals whose careers may be based outside traditional academic institutions.

Where Must Applicants Be Based?

Applicants must currently be residing in an African country.

For policy analysts and practitioners, the relevant organization or institution must also be based in Africa, including eligible:

  • Regional institutions.
  • Sub-regional institutions.
  • Government agencies.
  • Nongovernmental organizations.
  • Media organizations.
  • Civil society organizations.

The fellowship is therefore geographically focused on African professionals and African-based institutions.

What Areas of Research Does the Fellowship Support?

The APDD Individual Research Fellowship is intended for applicants working on issues related to conflict and peacebuilding.

The broader fellowship description also identifies peacebuilding, governance, and developmental dynamics as key areas.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed research demonstrates a clear connection to the fellowship’s thematic priorities.

Potential research questions may examine issues such as:

  • Conflict prevention.
  • Peacebuilding processes.
  • Post-conflict recovery.
  • Governance and peace.
  • Development and conflict.
  • Community-level peacebuilding.
  • Institutional responses to conflict.
  • Policy approaches to peace and stability.
  • Regional peace and security.
  • Civil society and peacebuilding.
  • Evidence-based approaches to conflict transformation.

The fellowship information provided does not prescribe a single research topic. Instead, applicants are expected to demonstrate how their proposed research contributes to the broader understanding of peacebuilding, governance, and developmental dynamics in Africa.

Fellowship Research Timeline

The fellowship follows a nine-month structure.

July 2026

The fellowship period begins, with fellows undertaking field-based research and participating in an APDD workshop.

July to December 2026

Fellows conduct approximately six months of field-based research.

During this period, fellows are expected to gather the evidence and information necessary to develop their research findings.

January 2027

Fellows participate in the second mandatory APDD workshop, which provides an opportunity to present findings, receive feedback, and consider how the research can be effectively disseminated.

January to March 2027

The final three months are dedicated to analysis and writing.

March 2027

The stated nine-month fellowship period concludes.

Applicants should note that the timeline described above comes directly from the program information provided and that the official application guide should be consulted for detailed expectations and scheduling.

How Much Funding Is Available?

In 2026, the APDD program plans to award up to nine individual fellowships.

Each fellowship carries a maximum award of $12,000.

If all nine fellowships are awarded at the maximum amount, the program could provide up to $108,000 in total fellowship awards.

Applicants should carefully review the official fellowship application guidebook for detailed information about eligible expenses, budget requirements, and how the proposed research budget should be prepared.

What Documents Are Required to Apply?

According to the fellowship information provided, applications consist of several important components.

Applicants should prepare:

  1. Online application form
  2. Research proposal
  3. Research bibliography
  4. Current CV
  5. Proposed research timeline
  6. Proposed research budget
  7. Two reference letters
  8. Language evaluation(s), if required

Each component plays an important role in demonstrating the applicant’s qualifications and the feasibility and significance of the proposed research.

Research Proposal

The research proposal is likely to be one of the most important parts of the application.

Applicants should use the proposal to clearly explain the research question or problem they intend to investigate, why the topic matters, how the research will be conducted, and how the expected findings can contribute to peacebuilding scholarship, policy, or practice.

A strong proposal should demonstrate a clear connection between the proposed research and the APDD program’s focus.

Bibliography

Applicants must also provide a bibliography supporting their proposed research.

The bibliography should demonstrate that the applicant understands the existing scholarship and relevant evidence surrounding the proposed research topic.

Current CV

Applicants must submit a current curriculum vitae.

The CV should clearly demonstrate the applicant’s relevant academic, professional, research, and peacebuilding experience.

For policy analysts and practitioners, the CV should be particularly useful in demonstrating the required five years of proven research and work experience in peacebuilding-related activities.

Research Timeline

Applicants must submit a proposed research timeline.

The timeline should demonstrate how the applicant intends to organize the research activities during the fellowship period.

A realistic timeline can help demonstrate that the proposed project is achievable within the fellowship’s nine-month structure.

Research Budget

Applicants must also submit a proposed research budget.

The budget should clearly explain how the requested fellowship support will be used to undertake the proposed research.

Applicants should ensure that their budget is realistic, clearly justified, and aligned with their proposed research activities.

Two Reference Letters

The application requires two reference letters.

Applicants should identify referees who can provide meaningful assessments of their academic, professional, research, or peacebuilding experience and their ability to successfully undertake the proposed fellowship research.

Language Evaluation

Language evaluation(s) may also be required where applicable.

Applicants should consult the official APDD Fellowship Application Guidebook to determine whether a language evaluation is necessary for their particular application.

How to Apply for the APDD Individual Research Fellowship

Interested applicants should consult the APDD Fellowship Application Guidebook for the complete application instructions and requirements.

The application involves an online application process and requires applicants to submit their research proposal, bibliography, CV, research timeline, budget, reference letters, and any required language evaluation.

Because the fellowship has specific eligibility requirements for academics, policy analysts, and practitioners, prospective applicants should carefully review the official guidance before beginning their application.

Applicants with technical questions about the online application portal can contact the APDD team by email at: apdd@ssrc.org

or visit their website HERE 

More fellowship opportunities can be found HERE

Fellowship Funding and Institutional Support

The APDD program is funded by the Andrew Carnegie Foundation.

The funding support allows the program to provide individual research fellowships while also facilitating workshops, mentorship, professional development, knowledge production, and networking opportunities for selected fellows.

The fellowship is administered through the Social Science Research Council, an organization focused on mobilizing social science research for the public good.

Why Should African Researchers and Peacebuilding Professionals Consider This Fellowship?

The APDD Individual Research Fellowship offers several potential advantages for professionals working in peacebuilding and related fields.

Financial Support for Research

The maximum fellowship award of $12,000 can provide significant support for an independent research project.

Dedicated Research Period

The nine-month structure provides fellows with dedicated time for field-based research, analysis, and writing.

Professional Visibility

Contributing to APDD publications, forums, and digital platforms can help fellows increase the visibility of their research and professional work.

Academic Publication Opportunities

Fellows may have opportunities to develop their work for peer-reviewed journals, books, articles, essays, blogs, features, and other forms of publication.

Mentorship

Access to experienced senior scholars can help fellows strengthen their research and professional development.

Networking

The fellowship connects participants with African scholars, practitioners, researchers, and other professionals working on peacebuilding issues.

Policy Impact

The program emphasizes research that can inform peacebuilding policy and practice, giving fellows an opportunity to connect their research with real-world challenges.

African Perspectives in Global Debates

The fellowship seeks to strengthen African voices and perspectives in regional and international discussions concerning peacebuilding.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Prospective applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements before preparing their applications.

In particular, academic applicants should verify their:

  • African citizenship.
  • Current residence in an African country.
  • Full-time faculty or research position.
  • Institutional affiliation.
  • PhD award date.

Policy analysts and practitioners should verify their:

  • African citizenship.
  • Current residence in Africa.
  • Institutional or organizational affiliation.
  • Master’s degree award date.
  • Five or more years of relevant research and work experience.
  • Experience specifically related to peacebuilding activities on the continent.

Applicants should also ensure that their proposed research has a strong connection to the fellowship’s focus on peacebuilding, governance, conflict, and developmental dynamics.

Application Deadline

No application deadline is provided in the information supplied for this article.

Applicants should therefore check the official APDD Fellowship Application Guidebook and application portal for the current deadline before submitting an application.

Prospective applicants should not assume a deadline based on previous editions of the fellowship, as application dates can change between competition cycles.

Contact Information

For questions or technical issues concerning the online application portal, applicants can contact the APDD team.

Email: apdd@ssrc.org

Applicants can also consult the following resources:

  • Individual Research Fellowship FAQs
  • APDD Fellowship Award Application Guidebook

About the Social Science Research Council

The Social Science Research Council (SSRC) is the organization behind the APDD Individual Research Fellowship.

The organization describes its mission as mobilizing social science for the public good.

The SSRC works to support research and knowledge that can contribute to understanding important social, political, economic, and developmental challenges.

The APDD fellowship reflects this broader mission by supporting African researchers and practitioners whose work addresses peacebuilding and related challenges across the continent.

Conclusion

The African Peacebuilding and Developmental Dynamics (APDD) Individual Research Fellowship 2026 represents a significant opportunity for African researchers, policy analysts, and practitioners working on conflict, peacebuilding, governance, and developmental dynamics.

With up to nine fellowships available and awards of up to $12,000 each, the program provides financial support alongside a broader professional development experience. Selected fellows will undertake six months of field-based research followed by three months of analysis and writing, participate in two mandatory APDD workshops, receive mentorship, build professional networks, and contribute to African and international knowledge production.

The fellowship is particularly suited to African academics with eligible PhD qualifications and full-time positions at African universities or research organizations, as well as experienced policy analysts and practitioners with the required master’s degree, organizational affiliation, and peacebuilding experience.

Beyond the financial award, the program offers an opportunity to strengthen research capacity, increase professional visibility, develop meaningful relationships with scholars and practitioners, and ensure that African evidence and perspectives contribute more strongly to peacebuilding policy and practice.

Interested applicants should carefully review the APDD Fellowship Application Guidebook, prepare all required application materials, verify their eligibility, and confirm the current application deadline before submitting their applications.

For technical questions regarding the application portal, prospective applicants can contact the APDD team at apdd@ssrc.org.
