item.content:encoded:
The University of Sydney offers a range of higher degree by research (HDR) opportunities for students seeking to undertake advanced academic research, including Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Joint PhD, Master’s by Research, and Master of Philosophy (MPhil) programs. These research degrees are designed for students who want to develop substantial expertise in a particular field while conducting an original research project under academic supervision.

For prospective research students, applying successfully involves more than simply submitting an online application. Applicants are expected to demonstrate previous research experience, strong academic performance, the ability to develop a meaningful research proposal, and a suitable relationship with a potential academic supervisor.

This comprehensive guide explains the University of Sydney postgraduate research application process, including eligibility requirements, research proposal development, finding a supervisor, required documents, application timing, scholarships and financial assistance, and additional requirements for international students.

University of Sydney Postgraduate Research Opportunities

A higher degree by research at the University of Sydney can include:

  • Doctor of Philosophy (PhD)
  • Joint PhD programs
  • Master’s by Research
  • Master of Philosophy (MPhil)

The University states that the general application process applies to most research courses and is intended for both domestic and international research students. However, individual faculties and schools may have additional admission requirements or variations in their procedures.

Applicants interested in research degrees in areas such as architecture, arts and social sciences, business, engineering and computer science, law, medicine and health, music, and science should therefore check the requirements of their intended course and faculty carefully.

Important Exception: Sydney Law School and Business School

Applicants interested in postgraduate research through the Sydney Law School or Business School should note that their application process differs from the general process.

For these schools, applicants first apply for their course. If they are successful, a supervisor will then be allocated to them. This differs from the general process, where applicants normally need to secure a supervisor before submitting their application.

Step 1: Check Your Eligibility

One of the most important parts of preparing an application is determining whether you meet the University’s academic and research requirements.

For postgraduate research study, the University states that applicants need previous research experience and a high academic record.

Previous Research Experience

Applicants should have completed a significant research project or thesis during their previous university-level studies.

Acceptable preparation may include:

  • An Australian honours degree
  • A master’s by research degree
  • A master’s by coursework that includes a substantial thesis or dissertation component

The purpose of this requirement is to demonstrate that applicants have already developed experience conducting academic research and are prepared for the demands of a higher research degree.

This means that prospective PhD or research master’s applicants should not focus only on their final grades. Their previous research experience is also an important part of demonstrating research capability.

Academic Requirements for Postgraduate Research

The University also places considerable importance on academic performance.

For the general postgraduate research requirements, applicants are expected to have a bachelor’s degree with first-class honours, with equivalent standards determined for students from other institutions. The University provides the following guide based on its grading system:

  • WAM of 75 over the degree
  • Honours Class I: WAM greater than 80
  • Honours Class II: WAM between 75 and 80

Equivalent qualifications from other institutions may be assessed according to the University’s requirements.

PhD Eligibility

Applicants seeking admission to a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) need to demonstrate sufficient previous research experience and capability.

In most cases, applicants will have one of the following:

  1. A bachelor’s degree with first-class honours;
  2. A master’s degree completed to a high academic standard that contains a substantial research component; or
  3. An equivalent qualification demonstrating research experience, academic excellence and research capability.

Therefore, prospective PhD applicants should be prepared to demonstrate not only academic excellence but also their ability to undertake independent and substantial research.

Eligibility for a Master’s by Research or Master of Philosophy

Applicants interested in a Master’s by Research or Master of Philosophy (MPhil) will generally need one of the following:

  • A bachelor’s degree with first- or second-class honours from the University of Sydney or another approved institution; or
  • An equivalent qualification demonstrating sufficient research experience and capability.

Applicants should still check the individual course requirements because specific faculties or programs may have additional admission criteria.

English Language Requirements

English language requirements vary depending on:

  • The specific course;
  • The applicant’s country of origin; and
  • Their previous educational background.

Applicants whose circumstances require proof of English proficiency should determine what evidence is required for their particular course.

International applicants should therefore check the English-language requirements well before submitting their application, particularly if their previous education was not conducted in English.

Joint PhD Opportunities

Students interested in a Joint PhD must initially follow Steps 1 to 3 of the University’s standard PhD application process.

There is an additional process for Joint PhD applicants. The proposed supervisor must complete a proposal to negotiate a student agreement form. If the proposal is accepted, the student must also sign an individual student agreement.

Once the student agreement has been finalised, the applicant will receive an application form for the Joint PhD program.

Applicants interested in this route should therefore allow additional time for discussions with their proposed supervisor and the formalisation of the relevant agreement.

Step 2: Develop a Strong Research Proposal

After establishing eligibility, the next major step is to develop a research proposal.

The University recommends carefully considering the subject of the proposed research project and beginning to develop a proposal that can be shared with potential academic supervisors.

A research proposal is important because it allows you to communicate:

  • What you want to research;
  • Why the topic is important;
  • What you intend to investigate;
  • Why your proposed research is worthwhile;
  • How the project relates to existing academic work; and
  • How your proposed research aligns with the research interests of a potential supervisor.

The University also notes that an initial proposal will likely evolve as discussions with the supervisor progress. Therefore, applicants should not necessarily expect their first version to be the final version.

The important point is to begin with a clear research idea and demonstrate why the proposed project is significant and appropriate for postgraduate research.

Step 3: Find a Suitable Research Supervisor

For most postgraduate research applications at the University of Sydney, applicants need to secure a supervisor before submitting their application.

The main exceptions are applicants to the Sydney Law School and Business School, where students apply for the course first and are allocated a supervisor if successful.

Finding an appropriate supervisor is therefore one of the most important stages of the application.

How to Search for a Supervisor

The University provides Sydney Profiles, where prospective research students can identify academics and explore research supervision opportunities.

Applicants can search using:

  • The name of a particular academic; or
  • A general keyword related to their research area.

For example, an applicant researching a particular scientific or engineering topic could use relevant keywords to identify academics working in that area.

The search can then be refined using filters such as:

  • Faculty and School;
  • Availability; and
  • Research supervision.

Applicants can also combine multiple keywords to make the search more specific.

What to Include When Contacting a Potential Supervisor

Finding an academic whose research interests match your proposed topic is only the beginning. Applicants should prepare a professional enquiry explaining why they are contacting that particular academic.

The University recommends providing information about:

  • Your academic background;
  • Your previous research experience;
  • The research topic you want to investigate;
  • How your proposed research aligns with the supervisor’s research;
  • Your CV or resume;
  • Academic transcripts for all degrees; and
  • Your initial research proposal.

This alignment is particularly important. A strong academic record alone does not necessarily demonstrate that a particular supervisor is suitable for your project. Your proposal should connect meaningfully with the academic’s research interests, projects or expertise.

Step 4: Submit the Application Online

Postgraduate research degree applications at the University of Sydney are open throughout the year.

However, most research intakes begin during:

  • Research Period 2 — March
  • Research Period 3 — July

Applicants should check the research periods available for their specific faculty and course because not every program necessarily follows exactly the same schedule.

The University recommends applying as early as possible before the intended start date.

Applicants should also discuss their intended start date with their proposed supervisor.

Is There a General Application Deadline?

The source does not state one single general deadline for all postgraduate research applications.

Instead, applications are described as being open throughout the year, while individual research periods and funding opportunities may have their own relevant dates.

Important Scholarship Deadline Consideration

Applicants who want to be considered for the Research Training Program (RTP) stipend must submit their application by the relevant RTP dates.

The University explains that applicants may still submit their course application after an RTP deadline, but their stipend outcome will not be provided until the next round of RTP rankings.

Therefore, students seeking funding should not wait until the last possible moment to submit their research degree application.

Deadline: No single general postgraduate research application deadline is stated in the provided source. RTP scholarship applicants must follow the applicable RTP dates.

Documents Required for a University of Sydney Research Degree Application

Once a supervisor has been secured and the research project has been refined, applicants need to prepare the required supporting documentation.

The University identifies several important categories of documents.

1. Research Proposal

The research proposal should be finalised in conjunction with the supervisor.

The University specifies a proposal of up to 2,000 words, covering the objectives and significance of the proposed research.

The proposal should therefore communicate the central purpose and value of the research project clearly.

2. Evidence of Supervisor Agreement

Applicants need evidence that a primary supervisor has agreed to supervise them.

This may take the form of email correspondence showing that the staff member has agreed to supervise the applicant.

The Sydney Conservatorium of Music may have an additional interview requirement.

3. Referee Reports

Applicants must provide two referee reports using the University’s specified forms.

Applicants should therefore identify appropriate academic referees in advance and allow enough time for them to complete and submit their reports.

4. Academic Transcripts

Applicants must provide official academic transcripts.

These transcripts need to be supplied:

  • In the original language; and
  • With an English translation where applicable.

5. English Language Evidence

Applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency if English is not their first language and the course requires such evidence.

6. CV or Resume

A curriculum vitae or resume is also required as part of the application documentation.

The CV should provide a clear picture of the applicant’s academic background and relevant research experience.

7. Additional Course-Specific Documents

Some courses may require additional materials.

Depending on the program, these could include:

  • A portfolio;
  • An audition; or
  • Other documents specified in the relevant course listing.

Applicants should therefore check their specific degree page rather than assuming that the general documentation list covers every requirement.

General Documents Applicants Need to Prepare

The application also requires proof of identity.

Examples include:

  • A valid passport biodata page;
  • An Australian birth certificate; or
  • An Australian or New Zealand citizenship certificate for domestic students.

Domestic applicants seeking part-time study also need to provide a statement demonstrating that they have sufficient time available to conduct their research under University supervision and complete the degree within the maximum permitted period for part-time PhD enrolment.

Additional Requirements for International Students

International applicants should pay particular attention to the additional requirements associated with studying in Australia.

According to the provided information, international students will need to address immigration and application requirements after receiving an admission offer or an electronic Confirmation of Enrolment (eCoE).

They will need to apply for the appropriate student visa after receiving the necessary admission documentation.

Application Processing Fee

International applicants are also required to pay a non-refundable application processing fee.

However, the source states that this fee can be waived in certain circumstances, including where:

  • The applicant is a sponsored student; or
  • A University staff member grants an exemption during an office interview or recruitment event.

International applicants may also use an authorised University of Sydney agent where appropriate. The University has partnered with authorised agents who can assist with applications and arrangements on behalf of students.

Scholarships and Financial Assistance for Postgraduate Research

Funding is an important consideration for students pursuing research degrees.

The University of Sydney states that it has one of the largest research scholarship schemes in Australia. Research scholarships may help students finance their research or meet living costs while undertaking their studies.

Scholarships may be:

  • Specific to a particular research project;
  • Specific to a particular discipline; or
  • Awarded based on academic merit and research potential.

This means that prospective applicants should investigate available funding opportunities alongside their course application.

Stipend Scholarships

The University also offers competitive stipend scholarships designed to provide an allowance that assists with living costs.

These awards are based on factors including:

  • Academic merit; and
  • Research potential.

Applicants seeking these scholarships must complete the additional scholarship form as part of the course application process.

Funding for Domestic Students

Domestic students do not pay tuition fees and are awarded an RTP Fees Offset under the Australian Government’s Research Training Program.

Funding for International Students

International students are required to pay tuition fees, with fee estimates available through the individual course pages.

However, international applicants can apply for scholarship packages that may provide:

  • A stipend scholarship to assist with relocation and living costs; and
  • A tuition fee scholarship.

These scholarship packages are described as highly competitive and have limited places.

Applicants who require financial assistance should therefore research funding opportunities early and pay close attention to scholarship-specific deadlines.

Research Ethics and Additional Approvals

Some research projects may involve additional ethical or institutional requirements.

For example, applicants conducting research involving fieldwork in the New South Wales hospital and education systems may be required to pass health and security checks. Additional admission criteria may also be specified by the individual course.

Depending on the nature of the research, students may also need approval from relevant ethics committees.

The University specifically notes that research involving human participants or animals may require approval from:

  • The Animal Ethics Committee; and/or
  • The Human Research Ethics Committee.

This is particularly important for applicants whose proposed research involves people, personal information, clinical environments, animals, or other ethically sensitive research activities.

Which Faculties Offer Postgraduate Research Opportunities?

The University provides faculty-specific information for postgraduate research across a wide range of academic disciplines.

Applicants can find additional information for:

  1. Architecture, Design and Planning
  2. Arts and Social Sciences
  3. Business
  4. Engineering and Computer Science
  5. Law
  6. Medicine and Health
  7. Music
  8. Science

Because individual faculties may have different admission requirements or application procedures, prospective students should use the relevant faculty or course page to confirm their requirements before applying.

How to Make Your Application Stronger

Although meeting the formal requirements is essential, prospective applicants should also approach the application strategically.

1. Start With a Clear Research Idea

Before approaching supervisors, develop a research idea that clearly identifies the issue you want to investigate.

Your idea should be specific enough to form the basis of a research project but flexible enough to evolve through discussions with your supervisor.

2. Demonstrate Research Experience

Previous research experience is a major component of the University’s eligibility requirements.

Applicants should therefore clearly communicate relevant:

  • Theses;
  • Dissertations;
  • Research projects;
  • Academic research experience; and
  • Other substantial research work.

3. Choose Supervisors Carefully

Do not simply contact academics because they work within your general discipline.

Instead, look for meaningful overlap between:

Your proposed research + the academic’s research expertise + the academic’s current research projects.

The University specifically encourages applicants to explain how their proposed research aligns with the work of their proposed supervisor.

4. Prepare Your Documents Early

Applicants should begin preparing transcripts, CVs, research proposals, referee reports and evidence of supervisor support well before the intended submission date.

This is especially important for international applicants who may also need to consider English-language evidence, application processing requirements and visa processing times.

The University recommends international applicants factor Department of Home Affairs visa processing times into their planning when considering a likely start date.

5. Consider Funding at the Same Time as Admission

Students who require financial support should not treat scholarship applications as an afterthought.

Because RTP and other scholarship opportunities can have separate deadlines and competitive ranking processes, applicants should investigate funding requirements before submitting their course application.

Application Timeline: What Prospective Students Should Do

A practical approach to the University of Sydney postgraduate research application process is:

Stage 1: Identify your research area

Determine the discipline and broad subject you want to investigate.

Stage 2: Confirm eligibility

Check your academic qualifications, research experience, academic performance and English-language requirements.

Stage 3: Develop an initial research proposal

Create a clear proposal explaining the research problem, objectives and significance.

Stage 4: Search for potential supervisors

Use Sydney Profiles to identify academics whose research interests align with your proposed project.

Stage 5: Contact potential supervisors

Send a professional enquiry accompanied by your CV, transcripts and initial research proposal.

Stage 6: Refine the research project

Work with the prospective supervisor to improve and finalise your research proposal.

Stage 7: Prepare supporting documentation

Gather transcripts, referee reports, proof of English proficiency where required, identity documents and any course-specific materials.

Stage 8: Apply online

Submit your postgraduate research application through the University’s online application process.

Stage 9: Apply for relevant funding

Complete the additional scholarship requirements if you wish to be considered for available research scholarships.

Stage 10: Prepare for additional requirements

International applicants should plan for visa requirements, while applicants whose research involves humans, animals or certain fieldwork environments should consider the relevant ethics and approval requirements.

Deadline for University of Sydney Postgraduate Research Applications

There is no single general deadline stated in the provided source for all postgraduate research degree applications.

Instead, applications are open throughout the year, with research intakes generally taking place in March and July. Applicants are advised to check their specific course and faculty requirements and apply as early as possible before their intended start date.

However, applicants seeking consideration for an RTP stipend must follow the applicable RTP submission dates. Applications submitted after the relevant RTP deadline may still be considered for admission, but the applicant’s stipend outcome will be considered in a subsequent RTP ranking round.

Deadline: No universal postgraduate research application deadline is specified in the source; scholarship applicants should check the applicable RTP and course-specific deadlines.

Who Can Apply?

The University of Sydney’s postgraduate research application process is available to both domestic and international research students.

Academic qualifications

Depending on the degree, applicants generally need:

  • Previous significant research experience;
  • A strong academic record;
  • Appropriate bachelor’s honours or master’s-level qualifications for PhD study; or
  • A bachelor’s degree with first- or second-class honours, or equivalent research capability, for a research master’s/MPhil.

LEARN MORE HERE

Geographic eligibility

The provided source does not identify a restricted list of countries or a particular continent from which applicants must come. It explicitly describes the process as being open to both domestic and international research students.

Race or ethnicity

The provided source does not specify a race or ethnic group restriction for postgraduate research admission.

International applicants

International students can apply, but they may have additional requirements involving:

  • English-language proficiency;
  • Application processing fees;
  • Student visa arrangements;
  • Tuition fees; and
  • Potential international scholarship opportunities.

Conclusion

Pursuing a postgraduate research degree at the University of Sydney can provide an opportunity to undertake advanced independent research through a PhD, Joint PhD, Master’s by Research or Master of Philosophy. However, applicants should understand that the process involves considerably more than completing an online form.

A competitive application begins with the right academic preparation and research experience, followed by the development of a strong research proposal and identification of an appropriate supervisor. Applicants then need to refine their project with their supervisor and prepare the required academic, research and personal documentation before submitting the application.

The University accepts postgraduate research applications throughout the year, although individual courses and research periods may have specific requirements. Students seeking scholarships, particularly RTP funding, need to pay close attention to the relevant funding deadlines because scholarship consideration may operate on a different timeline from general course admission.

For international applicants, additional planning is particularly important because English-language requirements, application fees, tuition costs, scholarships and visa processing may all affect the application timeline.

Ultimately, prospective applicants should begin early, carefully examine their intended course and faculty requirements, identify supervisors whose research aligns with their interests, develop a well-defined proposal, and prepare all supporting documentation before submission. With careful planning, the University of Sydney’s postgraduate research pathway can provide a structured route toward advanced academic research and higher-degree study.

LEAP Africa is inviting experienced, passionate, innovative, and values-driven professionals to explore career opportunities within an organisation focused on youth leadership development and sustainable transformation across Africa. Through its work as an ecosystem builder, thought leader, and development hub, LEAP Africa aims to empower the next generation of African leaders and contribute to lasting impact across communities.

For professionals interested in leadership, youth development, programme management, organisational transformation, and social impact, the organisation offers an opportunity to become part of a dynamic team working to expand its impact across the continent.

Among its current openings is the Director of Programmes position, a senior leadership opportunity based in Lagos, Nigeria.

Opportunity Overview

LEAP Africa describes itself as an institution working beyond the traditional role of an organisation. Its ambition is to serve as an ecosystem builder, thought leader, and development hub for young people across Africa.

The organisation places its people at the centre of this mission and seeks individuals who are prepared to contribute their skills, creativity, ideas, and leadership to initiatives focused on developing young African leaders.

The current Director of Programmes opening is particularly suited to an experienced professional who can provide strategic leadership for LEAP Africa’s programmes and help guide their development in line with the organisation’s priorities for 2027 and beyond.

Key Details

  • Position: Director of Programmes
  • Organisation: LEAP Africa
  • Employment type: Full-time
  • Location: Lagos, Nigeria
  • Application deadline: 20 September 2026
  • Application: Applicants can apply through the official application form provided by LEAP Africa.

Apply for the Director of Programmes position

About LEAP Africa

LEAP Africa presents itself as an organisation committed to developing young leaders and supporting sustainable transformation across African communities.
